[1. PURPOSE]
Korean fitness routine guide poster, A4 portrait instructional layout for home workout reference, gym wall posting, and social sharing.\nDark gym-style workout manual with numbered steps, practical pose diagrams, compact training specs, issue/date metadata, coach credit, and realistic printed-poster details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center layout: a tall editorial fitness poster with a strong workout title area at the top, a 5-step routine grid in the middle, and caution/info blocks plus guide metadata at the bottom.
- Background treatment: deep charcoal matte paper surface with subtle vignette, faint fitness-grain texture, light scuff marks, soft paper fibers, and realistic printed ink density while keeping all Korean copy readable.
- Add real guide-poster details: small top label “HOME TRAINING GUIDE”, issue tag “VOL.08”, date label “2026.05”, coach/model credit line “COACH 김도윤 · MODEL 이서준”, tiny barcode/QR-style area, page number “P.12”, and a short footer note “매주 3회 반복 권장”.
- Step cards should feel like a real gym magazine instruction page: evenly spaced, strong vertical rhythm, thin divider rules, small icon markers, compact captions, timing labels, and subtle paper-cut shadows.
- Each step gets a numbered label, pose illustration, short exercise caption, key muscle note, breathing cue, and mini repetition/time chip.
- Use {운동·부위}, {운동 단계}, {자세 일러}, {세트·시간}, {주의사항}, {강도}, {비주얼 결}, {컬러}, {비율} as editable placeholders in the layout copy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header: set the main guide title as a bold fitness manual masthead, then place {운동·부위} directly beneath it as the routine subject line. Add a compact magazine-style metadata row around the header: “VOL.08”, “2026년 5월호”, “LEVEL {강도}”, “10 MIN ROUTINE”.
- Routine grid (middle 65%): build a 5-step vertical sequence using {운동 단계}, with each step separated by thin rules and a clear numeric badge (01–05) in lime accent. Include short Korean micro-copy per card such as “호흡 유지”, “천천히 반복”, “복부 긴장”, “무릎 정렬”, “마무리 스트레칭”.
- Illustration zone: place {자세 일러} beside or under each step as simple silhouette or clean cartoon pose drawings, with consistent scale and identical visual weight across all five steps. Add small directional arrows, joint-angle markers, and muscle highlight patches in lime to make the guide feel instructional.
- Training spec strip: include {세트·시간} in a boxed info row, using concise labels and strong contrast for quick reading. Add supporting spec chips: “휴식 30초”, “준비물 매트”, “난이도 {강도}”, “권장 빈도 주 3회”.
- Warning block: place {주의사항} in the lower section with a caution icon style, separated from the main routine by a thin divider line. Include a realistic checklist style with tiny square bullets and short safety notes.
- Sponsor / guide footer area: add a small sponsor-style strip reading “FIT NOTE LAB · 홈트레이닝 자료실”, a QR-code placeholder block, barcode area, page number “P.12”, and tiny editorial credit text “디자인 {비주얼 결} · 출력비율 {비율}”.
- Intensity badge: show {강도} as a compact tag near the title or routine header, styled like a gym difficulty marker with lime outline and charcoal fill.
- Visual note and format footer: integrate {비주얼 결} and {비율} as small editorial metadata text, reinforcing that this is a structured guide poster.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard Bold for the main title, Pretendard SemiBold for step labels, Noto Sans KR Regular for supporting text, 22–44px hierarchy with compact line height; use small condensed English labels for metadata such as “ROUTINE”, “SET”, “CAUTION”, “CHECK”.
- Color palette: {컬러} with charcoal #1E1F22, lime green #B7F34A, white #F7F7F4, cool gray #A7AAB0, and muted ink-black #111214 for printed depth.
- Border/shadow: thin white or lime divider lines, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 14% opacity on step cards, subtle paper-edge shadow, fine halftone grain, and realistic matte print texture.
- Decorative graphic elements: use small arrows, pulse-line motifs, measuring ticks, circular step markers, tiny calendar and stopwatch icons, diagonal lime accent bands, and compact sponsor/footer blocks that support the workout-guide theme.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat graphic poster look inspired by a 24mm top-down editorial layout, rendered like a high-resolution photographed print using a Canon EOS R5 with 24mm lens, crisp vector-like clarity and controlled perspective.
- Lighting: even studio-style illumination with soft edge falloff, gentle paper texture highlights, slight edge contrast around icons and step cards for readability, and believable matte ink behavior.
- Color grade: dark charcoal base with lime accent pops and clean white text, high-contrast gym infographic palette, realistic printed blacks, and subtle cool-gray tonal variation.

[6. MOOD]
A practical fitness magazine instruction page — Men’s Health training guide meets modern gym infographic aesthetic, with the tactile realism of a premium printed workout poster pinned inside a clean urban gym.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "운동 루틴 사용설명서", "운동 {운동·부위}", "단계 {운동 단계}", "자세 {자세 일러}", "세트 {세트·시간}", "주의 {주의사항}", "강도 {강도}", "비주얼 {비주얼 결}", "컬러 {컬러}", "{비율}", "VOL.08", "2026년 5월호", "COACH 김도윤", "MODEL 이서준", "휴식 30초", "준비물 매트", "권장 빈도 주 3회", "P.12", "FIT NOTE LAB"
- Layout invariants: all 5 steps must be clearly numbered, pose illustrations must remain simple line-silhouette or simple cartoon style, and the dark gym aesthetic with lime accent must stay consistent throughout.
- The final image must read as a complete realistic Korean workout routine guide poster with title, metadata, step cards, specs, warning block, footer credit, QR/barcode-style area, and printed texture.

[1. PURPOSE]
K-beauty skincare routine guide poster, vertical A4-style manual for everyday use. Create a realistic printed beauty-magazine infographic photographed as a premium desk flat-lay, with step-by-step educational content, numbered routine cards, face and hand illustrations, product callouts, small editorial details, and practical reference labels for social sharing.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the main guide area in a tall editorial page layout, with {비주얼 결} as the core presentation style.
- Build a polished magazine-like grid with warm paper texture, visible printed ink, thin separators, layered label chips, small annotation arrows, and evenly spaced step cards so the sequence reads top-to-bottom with strong visual rhythm.
- Use {제품·종류} as the topical headline context, with {대상 피부} and {추천 시간} placed as smaller supporting labels near the title area.
- Keep the background as a soft cream paper surface with subtle warm texture, using {컬러} as the overall palette direction; add natural beauty-desk details such as soft product shadows, cream swatches, tiny cotton pads, a ceramic tray edge, and faint paper grain around the poster.
- Include realistic editorial micro-elements: issue label "BEAUTY ROUTINE NOTE VOL.247", date label "2026년 5월호", page code "SKINCARE / PAGE 08", a small barcode-style area, and a tiny QR-style square marked "루틴 저장".

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area (top 12-15%): title block with a bold K-beauty guide feel, followed by compact sublabels for {제품·종류}, {대상 피부}, and {추천 시간}. Add short Korean deck text such as "아침·저녁 루틴을 한눈에 정리한 단계별 체크리스트" plus small credit text "Guide Editor: 김하린 / Model Skin Type: {대상 피부}".
2. Step grid (middle 65-70%): arrange the full {단계 시퀀스} as vertically stacked numbered boxes, each box containing one small illustration and one short instruction line from {각 단계 설명}. Include tiny routine metadata within cards, such as "흡수 30초", "손바닥 온기", "목 라인까지", without replacing the provided step text.
3. Illustration treatment: each step card should pair a simplified hand-and-face diagram with a tiny product icon or bottle silhouette, showing where the product is applied and how it moves across the face. Add small realistic details like serum drops, toner pad texture, cream smears, cap highlights, and arrows following cheek, forehead, nose, and jaw movement.
4. Emphasis system: make the numbered steps the strongest visual cue with clear circular or rounded-square number markers, plus small Korean labels "STEP", "POINT", and "CHECK" to create a real printed manual feel; explanation text stays compact and easy to scan.
5. Side note column: add a slim right-side annotation rail with three short Korean tips: "피부 결 방향으로", "자극 없이 얇게", "충분히 흡수 후 다음 단계". Include tiny icons for morning, night, hydration, and barrier care.
6. Footer strip (bottom 10-12%): add a concise usage summary area that reinforces the routine flow and balances the composition like a modern beauty magazine infographic. Include checklist boxes, storage reminder "개봉 후 12개월 이내 사용 권장", contact-style text "@daily.beauty.note", and small publication line "Printed routine card for personal skincare log".

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the main Korean text, Bold 700 for the title, Medium 500 for labels, Regular 400 for step explanations; title around 34-44px, body around 18-22px, micro captions around 9-12px while remaining legible.
- Color palette: cream #F7F1E8, beige #E8D8C8, soft pink #F3D7DB, muted blush #E8BFC3, charcoal #2F2A28, warm gray #8A817C, with {컬러} guiding accent chips, number markers, and tiny product-label highlights.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px warm-gray rules, step cards with soft drop shadow 0px 4px 12px rgba(47,42,40,0.12), rounded corners 14-18px; add printed-paper edge shadow, faint page curl, and soft overlapping shadows from nearby skincare props.
- Graphic details: use elegant dividers, dotted measurement ticks, subtle ingredient-note tags, small swatch circles, arrow callouts, barcode block, QR-style square, and editorial footer metadata to make the poster feel like a real beauty guide page.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat-lay editorial composition photographed like a real printed poster on a beauty desk; Canon EOS R5 with RF 50mm f/2.8 macro, slight natural lens perspective, crisp printed typography, realistic paper grain, and product-shot shadows with minimal distortion.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left with gentle fill from right, producing even highlights, natural paper shadows, satin reflections on product icons, and warm depth around the page edges.
- Color grade: warm cream + powder pink + beige with restrained charcoal accents, slightly desaturated for a premium magazine-infographic look; preserve {컬러} as the dominant accent direction.
- Material realism: matte coated paper, lightly raised ink impression, faint toner texture in pale blocks, soft cosmetic smear textures, glass/plastic bottle reflections, and tactile stationery-like details.

[6. MOOD]
Premium K-beauty magazine infographic — a practical skincare routine guide like a Vogue Korea beauty spread mixed with a refined clinical user manual, made warmer and more lived-in with real desk textures, editorial microcopy, and beauty counter details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표시되어야 하는 문구: "화장품 사용 가이드 매뉴얼", "제품", "시퀀스", "설명", "대상", "시간", "비주얼", "컬러".
- Additional Korean text to render clearly: "BEAUTY ROUTINE NOTE VOL.247", "2026년 5월호", "아침·저녁 루틴", "루틴 저장", "피부 결 방향으로", "자극 없이 얇게", "충분히 흡수 후 다음 단계", "@daily.beauty.note".
- Step integrity: the guide must clearly show the full {단계 시퀀스} in correct order, with each step visually separated and easy to follow.
- Illustration integrity: every step card should include a face/hand-style illustration and a small product visual cue, matching the same layout rhythm across all steps.
- Preserve all placeholders exactly as written: {제품·종류}, {단계 시퀀스}, {각 단계 설명}, {대상 피부}, {추천 시간}, {비주얼 결}, {컬러}, {비율}.
- No broken Hangul, no distorted labels, no missing number markers.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean cookbook recipe card, vertical A4-style layout for a home-cooking recipe. Create a content-rich, realistic printable recipe page with an appetizing hero food photo, ingredient list, numbered step panels with small illustrations, prep metadata, kitchen-note details, and shareable magazine-card polish.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: food hero occupies the upper 38% of the frame, with {요리·인분} set as the main recipe title over or just below the photo. The ingredient list sits in a clearly separated left-side or lower-left block, and the step-by-step area fills the lower 42% with three numbered modules.
- Background treatment: warm cream paper texture with visible subtle grain, faint recipe-card fibers, charcoal text blocks, amber/red accent labels, light oil-splash speckles near the food area, and realistic printed-paper depth.
- Framing and reading flow: build a vertical editorial card with a top date strip, small recipe index number, prep icons, section tabs, and a footer line so it feels like a real saved recipe from a Korean home-cooking magazine.
- Include small supporting content: printed labels such as “오늘의 집밥”, “RECIPE CARD 024”, “2026.05 저장용”, “장보기 메모”, “완성 포인트”, and a tiny footer credit “photo · home kitchen / styling · seasonal table”.
- Use {요리·인분}, {재료}, {단계 1}, {단계 2}, {단계 3}, {조리 시간·난이도}, {팁}, {비주얼 결}, {컬러}, {비율} as editable content anchors.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero area (top 38%): present {요리·인분} as a large appetizing cooked-dish photo with realistic steam, glossy sauce or surface detail, visible garnish, ceramic plate texture, a spoon/chopsticks edge, linen napkin corner, and natural tabletop shadows. Add a small rounded badge reading “오늘의 집밥” and a tiny issue/date label “RECIPE CARD 024 · 2026.05”.
2. Ingredient area: arrange {재료} in a tidy vertical list with small bullet icons, miniature ingredient sketches, and grocery-note styling. Add a small header “재료 준비” plus a tiny sublabel “장보기 메모” and subtle divider ticks for quantities.
3. Step 1 panel: show {단계 1} as a numbered card labeled “01” with a small illustration or thumbnail of the key action, plus a tiny time icon and a short Korean micro-label such as “손질”.
4. Step 2 panel: show {단계 2} in the same style as Step 1, matching card size and icon treatment. Add light pan/steam line art or utensil marks that support the cooking action.
5. Step 3 panel: show {단계 3} as the final step card labeled “03” with slightly emphasized completion feel, a small plated-food thumbnail, and a micro-label such as “마무리”.
6. Info strip: place {조리 시간·난이도} as a concise metadata line near the title or above the step area, with icons for time, serving, and difficulty separated by dots or thin dividers. Include a small printed caption “조리 정보”.
7. Tip callout: highlight {팁} in a soft accent banner or note box with a folded-corner detail, using quotation marks exactly as provided and making it read like a handwritten kitchen memo. Add the label “셰프의 팁” or “완성 포인트”.
8. Visual system: apply {비주얼 결} across the full page so the composition reads as a polished Korean recipe magazine page with clear hierarchy, cute-but-refined step art, realistic paper and food textures, small editorial annotations, and practical recipe-card density.
9. Footer details: add a narrow bottom footer with “저장하고 다시 보기”, a tiny page marker “p.12”, small share/save-style micro icons, and decorative measuring-spoon or herb line art that matches {컬러} and {비율}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold for the main recipe title, Pretendard SemiBold for section headers, and Noto Sans KR Regular for body copy; title around 34–42px, section labels 18–22px, body 14–18px, micro labels 10–12px.
- Color palette: base the page on {컬러}, with cream paper #F4EEDF, charcoal #2E2A27, warm amber #D98B3A, and red accent #D94B45; keep contrast crisp and cookbook-readable.
- Border/shadow: use soft drop shadows with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity on cards; thin 1px divider lines in warm gray for structure; add small tab shapes, rounded labels, checkbox-style ingredient markers, and subtle paper-edge shading.
- Graphic details: include tiny utensil icons, steam strokes, ingredient doodles, a small recipe-number capsule, sticker-like accent tags, and measured spacing that feels editorial rather than sterile.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: styled like a high-end food editorial shot, 50mm f/2.8 on a full-frame camera for the hero dish, plus top-down flat-lay framing for ingredients and steps.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from the right, with subtle bounce light to keep the food glossy but natural; preserve believable shadows from plate rim, utensils, paper cards, and small ingredients.
- Color grade: warm cream + amber + muted red + charcoal, with slightly lifted highlights and clean midtone contrast for a home-style magazine finish.
- Material realism: show tactile paper grain, printed ink texture, ceramic glaze, food moisture, sesame/herb garnish detail, and small natural imperfections that make the recipe card feel photographed and printed.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean home-cooking editorial — like a polished recipe spread from a warm lifestyle magazine, practical enough to cook from, with cozy kitchen realism, small personal notes, and clear step-by-step clarity.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문자열이 정확한 한글로 보여야 함.
  - {요리·인분}
  - {재료}
  - {단계 1}
  - {단계 2}
  - {단계 3}
  - {조리 시간·난이도}
  - {팁}
- Additional Korean labels must be legible and natural: “오늘의 집밥”, “RECIPE CARD 024”, “2026.05 저장용”, “재료 준비”, “장보기 메모”, “조리 정보”, “셰프의 팁”, “완성 포인트”, “저장하고 다시 보기”.
- Layout invariants: hero food shot must be the primary focal point, ingredients must be clearly separated from steps, and the three step panels must remain numbered in order with small illustrations.
- Keep {비주얼 결}, {컬러}, and {비율} reflected in the overall editorial system, palette, and vertical recipe-card proportions.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Consumer electronics instruction manual cover or inner spread, A4 portrait editorial layout with clean technical documentation aesthetics.
Designed to look like a real appliance user guide for a premium home electronics brand, suitable for print-style product documentation, warranty booklet, quick-start sheet, or service-center PDF preview.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main product zone: {제품·모델} occupies the central 45–55% of the page, rendered as a clean product illustration with clear silhouette, part labels, button names, port labels, and technical callouts.
- Header and document identity: top 15–20% contains the manual title, model name, document code, revision date, customer-center line, QR code area, and a compact chapter list, aligned to a strict technical grid with thin rules.
- Background treatment: flat white paper texture with subtle off-white fiber grain, faint scan edge density, light fold/print registration marks, and realistic handbook paper feel.
- Spacing and framing: functional A4 documentation grid with boxed sections, left-aligned columns, side notes, numbered callouts, safety icons, small caption labels, and dense but readable information hierarchy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Title block (top 12%): brand-appropriate manual masthead using {브랜드 결}, set in bold Korean sans-serif with compact spacing, followed by “사용 설명서”, {제품·모델}, {문서번호}, {개정일}, and technical divider rules.
- Document utility strip: include a slim row for {고객센터}, {웹사이트}, QR code placeholder labeled “제품 등록 / 동영상 가이드”, barcode-style inventory mark, page marker “p.01”, and a small service memo field.
- Chapter overview (upper-mid band): {챕터 구성} presented as a neat numbered list inside thin rectangular chapter boxes, each box aligned to the same width with consistent padding and tiny guide icons.
- Main product illustration (middle 40%): {제품 일러} shown as a precise black line illustration on white paper, with fine annotation leader lines, tiny part labels, numbered callouts, ventilation/connector details, scale ticks, and a small “각 부 명칭” caption.
- Step diagrams (lower-mid band): {단계별 일러} arranged as 3–5 small sequential panels with arrows, step numbers, short Korean captions, screw/plug/remote-control icons, and consistent line weight.
- Warning block (lower 15%): {주의사항} inside a bordered warning area with a red caution triangle icon, dense but legible Korean text, warranty notice, water/electricity/child-safety icons, and a clear manual-like hierarchy.
- Footer utilities (very bottom): {보증문구}, {주소}, disposal/recycling note, service reference line, small page number, and compact typographic rules consistent with a consumer electronics handbook.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for body and labels, 400–700 weight, 8–16px size range; use bold condensed Korean sans for headers, with tight but readable line spacing.
- Color palette: {컬러} plus paper white #F7F7F2, charcoal #222222, warning red #D83A3A, soft gray #B8B8B8, and a restrained brand accent tone for chapter numbers, QR label, and section tabs.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px black rules, crisp chapter boxes, precise table cells, small registration ticks, and a faint print-scanned paper edge shadow that makes the page feel physically scanned.
- Information density: real manual realism with labels, microcopy, table rows, icon captions, checklist boxes, serial-number sticker area, and footer references; all text should remain organized and readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: straight-on document scan look, equivalent to a high-resolution flatbed scan / 50mm perspective with zero distortion, exact orthographic page framing.
- Lighting: even diffuse studio light from directly above, no directional drama, no hotspots, no vignetting, paper surface evenly exposed.
- Color grade: neutral documentary whites, charcoal black linework, restrained red warnings, accurate print-like contrast, and subtle scanned-paper warmth.

[6. MOOD]
Real consumer electronics instruction manual — Epson / Panasonic product booklet clarity with Japanese technical catalog precision, Korean service-center practicality, and Scandinavian editorial restraint.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표시되어야 하는 문자열: “사용 설명서”, “01 안전·주의”, “02 설치”, “03 사용법”, “04 청소”, “05 문제 해결”, “⚠ 전기·물·어린이 안전 + 보증 정보”.
- 반드시 포함할 실제 문서 요소: “{문서번호}”, “{개정일}”, “{고객센터}”, “제품 등록 / 동영상 가이드”, “각 부 명칭”, “p.01”.
- Layout invariants: A4 세로 매뉴얼 페이지, 검정 라인 제품 일러스트, 챕터 박스, 단계별 패널, 빨간 경고 블록, QR/바코드 영역, 촘촘한 한글 설명문.
- Product depiction must feel like a real appliance manual, with exact technical organization, legible labels, document-control details, and practical service information.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Blurry illegible text
- Celebrity composites or unrelated human portraits

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean pharmaceutical instruction sheet, A4-vertical manual layout, public-facing medication guide with clear dosage, safety information, revision metadata, pharmacy contact details, and patient-friendly pictograms.
Trustworthy healthcare reference sheet style with compact typography, table-like structure, realistic leaflet microcopy, barcode/QR area, and warning emphasis.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the page as an A4 medication leaflet captured flat from above, with a practical outer margin of 6–8%, dense but readable information blocks, and realistic printed-paper grain.
- Use {약품명·종류} as the main title zone near the top, followed by stacked instructional sections for {복용법}, {용량}, {주의사항}, {부작용}, and {보관}.
- Add realistic document metadata: {문서번호}, {개정일}, {제조사}, {약국명}, {상담전화}, {처방번호}, plus a small barcode/QR-style verification box labeled for patient reference.
- Keep hierarchy separated with thin gray divider lines, small medical pictograms, numbered caution markers, dosage table cells, and footer notes that resemble a real Korean pharmacy handout.
- Use {비주얼 결} to guide icon density, small Korean typography, practical leaflet organization, and the balance between text blocks and diagrammatic elements.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area (top 12–15%): place "약품 복용 안내" as the document title, with "약품 {약품명·종류}" directly beneath; include {문서번호}, {개정일}, and a small right-side barcode/QR block.
2. Pharmacy / reference strip (below header 6–8%): show {약국명}, {처방번호}, {제조사}, and {상담전화} in a narrow information band with small phone, clipboard, and capsule icons.
3. Dosage section (upper-middle 18–22%): present {복용법} in a numbered or bullet format, with timing, frequency, and duration visually separated by dot icons, clock symbols, or vertical separators.
4. Amount section (middle 15–18%): show {용량} in a boxed dosage table, with adult/child dosage split into two rows and emphasis on milligram values, tablet count, and age notes.
5. Warning section (lower-middle 18–22%): display {주의사항} using a red warning icon, bold caution label, compact list formatting, triangular hazard pictograms, and small exclamation markers.
6. Side effect section (lower-middle 12–15%): present {부작용} as a concise alert block with a red or dark charcoal emphasis line, symptom icons, and a follow-up instruction line.
7. Storage section (bottom 10–12%): show {보관} in a footer-style area with green safety icon, temperature pictogram, child-safety symbol, and short storage guidance.
8. Footer microcopy: add a fine-print note reading "증상이 지속되면 의료진과 상담하세요" and a page marker "1/1" with a small revision code matching the medical leaflet style.
9. Color application: use {컬러} consistently for warning emphasis, safety cues, linework, icon accents, section labels, and small administrative labels while keeping the paper field predominantly white.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for body text at small but readable size, bold 700–800 for headers, regular 400–500 for body, with tight line spacing and clean medical-manual alignment.
- Color palette: {컬러}, plus off-white paper #F8F8F6, neutral gray #6B7280 for separators, and deep charcoal #1F2937 for body text.
- Layout details: thin 1px gray rules, clear table cells, compact label chips, realistic ink density, subtle paper-edge shadow at 8% opacity, and small icon illustrations that support the medication instructions.
- Printed realism: include slight toner variation, crisp but natural paper texture, tiny registration marks, barcode lines, and QR-like square modules without claiming official certification.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: high-resolution overhead scan look, 50mm normal lens perspective, perfectly flat document capture, no distortion, crisp print edges.
- Lighting: diffuse studio softbox from directly above with even coverage, gentle paper texture visibility, controlled reflections, and natural printed-document contrast.
- Color grade: clean white + charcoal + red warning accents + green safety accents, with practical hospital-pharmacy leaflet color balance and clear patient-guide readability.

[6. MOOD]
Clinical, authoritative, and practical — Korean hospital pharmacy handout, patient medication leaflet, and regulatory instruction manual feel with realistic administrative details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: "약품 복용 안내", "약품 {약품명·종류}", "복용 {복용법}", "용량 {용량}", "주의 {주의사항}", "부작용 {부작용}", "보관 {보관}".
- 추가로 선명하게 보여야 하는 문구: "문서번호 {문서번호}", "개정일 {개정일}", "조제 약국 {약국명}", "처방번호 {처방번호}", "제조사 {제조사}", "고객상담실 {상담전화}", "증상이 지속되면 의료진과 상담하세요", "1/1".
- Anatomy/layout invariants: all Korean characters must be clean and unbroken, text must remain legible at small size, pictograms must support the instructions, dosage table and numbered warning blocks must be present, and the overall layout must read like an official-looking medication manual without using fake certification marks.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public figures
- Text-obscuring illustrations or illegible dosage information

Clear technical documentation page with numbered build steps, part callouts, revision information, barcode/QR block, safety notes, customer-support footer, and small print details, designed to look like a real printed furniture instruction sheet included in a box.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Page layout: single A4 vertical sheet, dense but readable manual composition, structured grid with header, document metadata, parts legend, stacked assembly panels, caution box, support footer, page number, and barcode area.
- Main subject: {제품모델명} shown as simplified technical line illustration, centered across the middle 55% of the page, with exploded-view parts, assembly arrows, screw callouts, alignment marks, and repeated part references.
- Header details: include product title {제품모델명}, document code {문서번호}, revision/date line {발행일}, language mark “한국어”, and small page indicator {페이지표기} near the top-right.
- Parts area: {필요부품} placed as a compact legend block in the upper third, each part drawn as a small outlined icon with matching letter labels, quantity numbers, and a tiny “구성품 확인” checklist row.
- Step flow: {단계1}, {단계2}, {단계3}, {단계4} arranged in four numbered blocks from top to bottom, each block using a clean diagram, arrow guidance, part references, small tool icons, and short Korean instruction captions.
- Warning block: {주의사항} set in a dedicated caution box near the lower section with a yellow highlight bar, black iconography, safety pictograms, estimated time, and two-person assembly reminder.
- Footer content: include {고객센터}, {매장주소}, {QR안내}, a small barcode-like block, recycling symbol, tiny print line, and “다음 페이지 계속” style navigation cue.
- Background treatment: flat white printed paper with subtle off-white tint (#FAFAF7), faint scanner grain, light fold impression, tiny registration marks, and believable ink texture.
- Spacing and framing: strict grid alignment, thin dividing rules, consistent label placement, compact technical annotations, and functional manual-style boxes.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area (top 12%): title lockup using {제품모델명} in bold black sans-serif, small subtitle “조립 설명서”, document metadata {문서번호}, {발행일}, language mark, and {페이지표기}.
2. Parts legend area (upper 20%): present {필요부품} as outlined component drawings with letter tags A/B/C/D and Allen key icon, quantity badges, checkboxes, and a small “개봉 후 부품 수량을 먼저 확인하세요” note.
3. Assembly Step 1 panel (middle 16%): show {단계1} as a simple line diagram of leg and base connection, with one direction arrow, Allen key rotation icon, and a numbered circle for step 1.
4. Assembly Step 2 panel (middle 16%): show {단계2} placing the leg-base subassembly at the tabletop corners, with perspective alignment marks, corner guides, and part letters repeated on the drawing.
5. Assembly Step 3 panel (middle 17%): show {단계3} tightening four screws per leg, using fastener callouts, torque caution icon, rotational arrow symbols, and “x4” repeated markers.
6. Assembly Step 4 panel (lower 13%): show {단계4} flipping the furniture and checking surface stability, with final checkmark diagram, balance icon, felt-pad placement cue, and a small “완성” label.
7. Warning / notes / footer area (bottom 14%): place {주의사항} in a boxed caution strip with yellow accent, then include {고객센터}, {매장주소}, {QR안내}, barcode block, recycling mark, {페이지표기}, and tiny document control text.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a clean sans-serif similar to Noto Sans KR + Helvetica Neue, bold 18–22px for the main title, regular 10–13px for instructions, 8–9px for footer metadata, compact numeric labels, crisp vector-like text.
- Color palette: white #FFFFFF, off-white #FAFAF7, black #111111, IKEA-style yellow #FFCC00 for warnings and key callouts, neutral gray #D9D9D9 for divider lines, light blue #0058A3 only for tiny document-code accents if needed.
- Line and print treatment: thin 1px black rules, simple outlined boxes, consistent stroke weight, slightly imperfect printed ink edges, faint paper-edge shading, tiny crop/registration marks, and believable scanned-paper texture.
- Graphic treatment: monochrome line art with consistent stroke weight, filled black arrows, simple numbered circles, part labels in uppercase alphanumerics, exploded-view diagrams, torque arrows, and small safety/recycling pictograms.
- Realism details: include a barcode-like rectangle, QR-style square, revision code, page number, tiny Korean footer text, checklist boxes, and enough micro-labels to make the sheet feel manufactured and printed.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: orthographic technical illustration look, as if captured by a flatbed scanner; no photographic perspective, no depth-of-field blur, no lens distortion.
- Lighting: even top-down studio lighting, fully diffused and shadowless, like a scanned printed manual sheet.
- Color grade: clean print reproduction with neutral white paper, saturated warning yellow accents, crisp black ink, and subtle gray paper grain.

[6. MOOD]
Practical Scandinavian flat-pack manual — authentic furniture assembly booklet aesthetic, precise, useful, slightly industrial, with believable product-document metadata and printed instruction-sheet details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- 반드시 정확히 표시할 한국어 문구: “조립 설명서”, “제품·모델명”, “필요 부품”, “구성품 확인”, “단계 1”, “단계 2”, “단계 3”, “단계 4”, “주의사항”, “완성”, “고객센터”, “다음 페이지 계속”.
- 실제 설명서처럼 보이도록 {문서번호}, {발행일}, {페이지표기}, 바코드 영역, QR 안내, 재활용 표시, 작은 주석, 수량 체크박스가 함께 보여야 한다.
- 모든 도식은 기계적으로 그럴듯해야 하며, 부품 문자 A/B/C/D, 나사 수량, 화살표 방향, 단계별 조립 순서가 범례와 일치해야 한다.
- 한국어 글자는 깨끗하고 읽을 수 있어야 하며, 제목·단계명·주의 문구는 특히 선명해야 한다.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or human likeness focus

[1. PURPOSE]
Tesla-inspired futuristic sci-fi advertising poster / premium catalog visual with a real urban-night campaign atmosphere. The image should feel like a high-budget launch poster for next-generation mobility, technology, or lifestyle design, using cinematic contrast, precise reflections, and editorial information layers rather than a sterile mockup.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} placed as the hero element, occupying about 55–65% of the frame width, with strong separation from the background and realistic contact shadows/reflections.
- Background: a dark futuristic city-night scene with reflective wet pavement, glass towers, LED transit lines, distant traffic bokeh, subtle street haze, and neon architectural geometry; depth layers should guide the eye to the subject first.
- Framing: centered or slightly low-angle hero composition with an editorial poster grid. Include functional campaign details around the subject: issue/date label, small spec callouts, barcode/QR-style block, and a lower information band.
- Brand tone: {브랜드 톤·시그니처} should guide every visual decision, from contrast level to edge highlights, futuristic restraint, premium surfaces, and high-tech graphic rhythm.
- Poster realism: add small believable production details such as tiny credit text, location/date label, catalog code, sponsor strip, and a thin vertical spine note like a printed campaign board.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero zone (center, mid 60%): render {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} with crisp silhouette edges, polished surface reflections, high-end industrial finish, and realistic environmental reflections from city lights and wet ground.
- Background layer (full frame): build a nocturnal cityscape with glowing building lines, distant traffic bokeh, maglev or EV charging silhouettes, glass facades, small pedestrians or scale elements if appropriate, thin atmospheric fog, and dark graphite surfaces with controlled neon accents.
- Foreground detail layer: include wet asphalt or polished concrete texture, reflected cyan/red light streaks, subtle puddles, fine road markings, floor grid lines, and tiny floating dust/haze particles catching the light.
- Light accents: place cyan and red rim lights along subject edges and nearby structures to create Tesla-like contrast, while keeping highlights sharp, selective, and physically believable.
- Title area (upper or lower third): set {타이포·카피} as a bold sans-serif Korean headline, with smaller supporting Korean subcopy such as “미래 이동성의 새로운 기준”, “도심 야간 테스트 공개”, and “전동화 디자인 스페셜”.
- Editorial info: add short poster/catalog details in Korean: “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “SEOUL NIGHT DRIVE”, “촬영지: 서울 스마트 루프”, “모델 크레딧: {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)}”, and a small price/code line like “CATALOG ₩7,500 / CODE TX-0526”.
- Lower band: include date/time/venue-style event text such as “2026.05.24 20:30”, “서울 모빌리티 라운지”, “온라인 사전 공개”, plus a small barcode area and QR-like square graphic treated as printed poster information.
- Layout structure: {레이아웃} should feel editorial and commercial at once, with the subject dominating the composition while city scale, typography, spec cards, and campaign microtext create a complete premium advertisement.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use bold geometric sans-serif such as Pretendard Bold or Inter Black for the headline, with Noto Sans KR Medium for the Korean subline; headline size large, tight tracking, sharp alignment, and clean high-tech hierarchy.
- Korean copy integration: render short, legible Korean text blocks as part of the poster, including “미래 이동성의 새로운 기준”, “전동화 디자인 스페셜”, “도심 야간 테스트 공개”, “예약 공개 2026.05.24”, and “서울 스마트 루프”.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트} plus deep charcoal, graphite black, electric cyan, signal red, and clean white highlights; saturation should feel premium and cinematic, not cartoonish.
- Graphic system: add thin measurement lines, small spec tags, translucent HUD-style panels, subtle diagonal cuts, fine grid overlays, and micro labels that look printed into a real campaign layout.
- Border/shadow: subtle soft shadow under the hero subject, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; precise edge lighting and reflection falloff should define the form.
- Surface treatment: glossy metal, glass, carbon-like panels, tire rubber or fabric/leather if relevant, polished concrete, wet asphalt, and mirror-like reflections with faint specular streaks.
- Poster production details: include a small vertical spine text such as “FUTURE MOBILITY CATALOG / VOL.247”, tiny photographer/creative credit “Creative Direction: AURORA STUDIO”, a sponsor/support strip, and a barcode/QR-style information block.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm cinema lens at f/2.8 for a bold ad-poster perspective, or 50mm at f/4 if the subject needs a cleaner commercial look; slight low-angle framing for authority.
- Lighting: dramatic nocturnal lighting with a strong key from upper-left, cyan rim from right, and a subtle red accent backlight; add soft volumetric haze to separate city, subject, and foreground layers.
- Color grade: deep black shadows, cool cyan highlights, restrained red accents, clean whites, wet-surface reflections, and a high-contrast futuristic grade with realistic tonal rolloff.
- Realism: cinematic commercial photography look with physically plausible reflections, correct perspective, authentic scale cues, and detailed environment texture.

[6. MOOD]
High-end Tesla-style futuristic campaign visual — sleek industrial sci-fi with a cinematic commercial finish, like a premium auto brand launch poster photographed in a real neon city at night. The final image should feel rich, believable, editorial, and ready for a magazine spread or outdoor billboard.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear exactly as written: {브랜드 톤·시그니처}, {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)}, {컬러 팔레트}, {라이팅·무드}, {타이포·카피}, {레이아웃}, {비율}.
- Additional visible Korean text should be short and cleanly rendered, for example: “미래 이동성의 새로운 기준”, “전동화 디자인 스페셜”, “도심 야간 테스트 공개”, “예약 공개 2026.05.24”, “서울 스마트 루프”, “VOL.247”.
- Preserve a Tesla-inspired visual identity through composition, contrast, aerodynamic geometry, refined typography, and cinematic electric lighting language.
- Any human subject, if present, must be anatomically correct, naturally posed, and integrated into the environment with believable lighting and scale.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals/certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Niji-inspired modern anime key visual for a vertical campaign poster, advertisement, or premium catalog-cover style layout, with bold editorial impact and high-energy color storytelling.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: {주인공} appears as the dominant hero occupying about 60–70% of the frame, posed with strong diagonal energy, sharp silhouette, expressive face or product presence, and dramatic foreground depth cues.
- Background treatment: deep dark backdrop with layered gradient planes, anime speed-line geometry, holographic shards, small signage fragments, light streaks, and crisp graphic accents based on {컬러팔레트}.
- Poster information structure: place the oversized main headline {메인카피} in the upper or side headline field, a smaller subtitle {부제} beneath it, and event information blocks for {행사일시}, {장소}, and {티켓정보} near the lower third.
- Commercial realism: add a small sponsor/support area reading {후원표기}, a social handle {채널핸들}, compact QR-like graphic detail, serial code, and thin editorial labels to make the poster feel like a real printed campaign asset.
- Customizable identity cues: translate {브랜드결} into facial styling, outfit details, weapon/tool/product highlights, emblem patches, accessory tags, or luminous graphic motifs while keeping the look sharply modern anime.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero area: render {주인공} as the focal point with crisp anime linework, hard cel-shaded planes, controlled highlights, and a high-contrast silhouette that reads instantly at poster and thumbnail size.
2. Color structure: build the scene around saturated core colors from {컬러팔레트}, with deep anchor tones in the background, vivid neon accent flashes, and small warm highlights for emotional punch.
3. Lighting pass: apply {조명무드} as hard-edged cel-shaded illumination, with a clear key-light direction, pronounced shadow planes, rim lighting, and reflective accents on hair, clothing, props, or product surfaces.
4. Typography hierarchy: create a bold display title for {메인카피}, a subtitle line for {부제}, compact date/location/ticket blocks, and micro labels such as campaign code, “SPECIAL VISUAL”, and “LIMITED POSTER EDITION”.
5. Poster details: include decorative graphics based on {장식모티프}, small sponsor boxes, ticket notice, channel handle, thin divider rules, angled stickers, and layered editorial captions that support the hero rather than flattening the scene.
6. Layout finish: use {레이아웃} as a dynamic vertical poster arrangement with angled motion cues, asymmetrical balance, layered type, dramatic crop, and a polished anime campaign finish.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use bold display fonts such as Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the main headline, with subtitle and metadata in Noto Sans KR Medium; title should take roughly 15–22% of the vertical space, while event information uses compact but legible label blocks.
- Rendered poster text: combine large Korean headline typography with small English editorial tags, for example “KEY VISUAL”, “EP.00”, “SPECIAL NIGHT”, and “ONLINE TICKET”.
- Color palette: use the energy of {컬러팔레트}, guided by deep charcoal #11131A, electric cyan #24D7FF, neon magenta #FF4FD8, vivid red #FF3B30, and highlight white #F5F7FF.
- Border/shadow: add a refined poster-edge frame, decisive drop shadow around the hero (4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity), sharp cel-shaded shadow cutoffs, and small glossy print-like highlight streaks.
- Realistic print cues: include subtle paper grain, ink density variation, micro registration marks, tiny serial text, QR-like square detail, and sponsor/ticket rows that make the visual feel like a printed campaign poster.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: digital illustration with a cinematic 50mm-equivalent framing feel, shallow depth separation cues, and poster-composition precision rather than a photographic blur model.
- Lighting: hard key light from upper-left at about 45°, strong shadow blocks on the opposite side, subtle neon edge light from lower-right, and controlled reflective accents on hair, clothing, props, or product surfaces.
- Color grade: high-saturation anime campaign grade with deep blacks, cyan-magenta contrast, selective warm highlights, intense cel-shaded contrast, and a premium print-ad finish.

[6. MOOD]
A premium modern anime campaign visual — inspired by high-end Japanese pop-culture key art, with the sharp graphic confidence of a cinema poster, the intensity of an editorial magazine cover, and the practical information density of a real event poster.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered image must preserve these Korean strings exactly when used:
  - 메인 타이틀: “{메인카피}”
  - 부제: “{부제}”
  - 캠페인명: “{캠페인명}”
  - 행사 일시: “{행사일시}”
  - 장소: “{장소}”
  - 티켓 정보: “{티켓정보}”
  - 후원 표기: “{후원표기}”
  - 채널 핸들: “{채널핸들}”
- Layout invariants: keep {주인공} visually dominant, keep {메인카피} immediately readable, and make the event/date/ticket information feel intentionally designed rather than randomly placed.
- The final image should feel like a real 1024x1536 vertical anime campaign poster for {캠페인명}, with strong contrast, dramatic character energy, and finished commercial typography.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

[INPUT]
- language: Korean

[1. PURPOSE]
Classic hand-painted Japanese nature anime advertising poster / catalog visual with a handcrafted watercolor feel, lush environment storytelling, and the believable completeness of a printed promotional poster.
Vertical hero composition for promotional use, blending soft cinematic fantasy atmosphere with real poster details such as event information, sponsor marks, small credits, ticket guidance, and carefully integrated Korean copy.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} occupies the central 55–65% of the frame as the hero, surrounded by layered foliage, sky, small flowers, drifting leaves, insects, stones, moss, and atmospheric environment cues that make the scene feel lived-in.
- Background treatment: hand-painted nature landscape with mossy greens, warm amber highlights, soft cloud shapes, distant hills or forest paths, tiny birds, textured watercolor paper grain, and subtle brush pooling; the environment should feel expansive and story-rich.
- Framing and spacing: use asymmetrical balance with foreground leaves, tall grass, wildflowers, tree branches, and warm light patches framing the lower corners and side edges while keeping the hero readable.
- Poster information layer: include a believable lower information block with date/time/venue, ticket info, sponsor area, small contact line, and a tiny QR-style ticket box or barcode-like area, all harmonized with the illustration.
- Overall visual language: {브랜드 톤·시그니처} should feel like an original fantasy nature illustration with gentle whimsy, tactile paper texture, and warm narrative detail rather than a sterile mockup.
- Palette control: anchor the image with {컬러 팔레트} while keeping shadows soft and organically blended.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero focal area (center 60%): {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} rendered as the clear focal point, with soft painted edges, delicate highlights, and subtle depth separation from the background.
2. Environmental wrap (outer 20–25%): layers of trees, hills, leaves, flowers, mushrooms, grass, floating seeds, birds, or gentle wind lines encircle the hero to create a storybook world with natural perspective.
3. Light and atmosphere pass: {라이팅·무드} applied as diffused, painterly illumination with gentle bloom, faint haze, warm rim glow, and luminous edge highlights on foliage and the hero.
4. Typography zone: integrate {타이포·카피} as a strong Korean poster headline, with smaller supporting text such as “자연 anime”, “영문 부제”, “숲이 들려주는 하루”, and a short caption like “바람과 빛이 머무는 순간”.
5. Event / catalog detail zone: add realistic poster microcopy in Korean, for example “2026.05.24 SAT 14:00”, “초록숲 문화정원”, “입장권 ₩7,500”, “예매 문의 02-123-4567”, “주최: 숲빛기획”, “협찬: 그린마켓 · 달빛문구”, plus a small ticket box or QR-style square.
6. Layout discipline: {레이아웃} should remain editorial and poster-like, with the hero clearly dominant and supporting elements arranged in layered depth, like a finished promotional print.
7. Format constraint: maintain the vertical 1024x1536 composition with the main subject fully visible and not crop-cut.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: rounded Korean lettering with friendly editorial presence, using Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Bold for Korean and a clean sans-serif for English subcopy; headline size large, subtitle size medium, tracking slightly open.
- Korean copy hierarchy: set the main headline from {타이포·카피}; include smaller labels such as “자연 anime”, “영문 부제”, “2026 봄 숲 포스터”, “VOL.024”, and “poster credit: illustration by forest studio” as natural printed details.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트} plus muted cream highlights, deep forest green shadows, warm honey-amber accents, faded ink black, and soft paper beige; avoid neon saturation.
- Poster artifact: add subtle printed-paper grain, watercolor bloom, tiny ink misregistration, gentle edge wear, and a soft paper-edge shadow around 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 12–15% opacity.
- Surface feel: visible watercolor paper texture, soft brush transitions, hand-painted natural gradients, and small illustrated decorative motifs such as leaf icons, seed dots, wind swirls, and botanical dividers.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: medium-format editorial framing, Phase One IQ4 look with 80mm equivalent perspective, shallow-to-moderate depth separation, poster illustration adaptation rather than literal photography.
- Lighting: diffused overcast daylight with a warm bounce from lower-right, gentle rim glow on foliage edges, and no harsh specular highlights.
- Color grade: lush moss green, tea-amber, muted sky blue, and soft cream; preserve storybook contrast with slightly lifted shadows.
- Detail rendering: combine anime-style character/object clarity with painterly watercolor backgrounds, fine pencil-like contour lines, layered translucent washes, and believable printed catalog/poster finishing.

[6. MOOD]
Hand-painted nature fantasy anime mood — calm, lyrical, nostalgic, and warm, like a printed forest event poster found at a small local bookstore or garden café, with emotional softness, gentle whimsy, and a lived-in seasonal atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear exactly as written if text is rendered: “자연 anime”, “영문 부제”.
- Additional Korean poster details should be legible and realistic: “2026.05.24 SAT 14:00”, “초록숲 문화정원”, “입장권 ₩7,500”, “예매 문의 02-123-4567”.

- Masthead zone (top 8–12%): Place {매거진마스트헤드} in large fashion-editorial type, spanning most of the width, with issue metadata nearby: {이슈번호}, {발행일}, {가격}.

- Barcode and credit zone (bottom corner and spine edge): Add a realistic barcode block with {바코드번호}; add vertical spine credit text along one edge: {스파인크레딧}.

- Color grade: monochrome-dominant grade with restrained warm gold highlights and neutral blacks, inspired by high-fashion magazine reproduction.

Premium fashion editorial — dark luxury runway mood, dramatic magazine-cover presence, sophisticated Korean fashion issue energy, and confident black-and-gold visual authority.

[7. CRITICAL]

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

Hero image — Place {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} as the focal subject, cleanly separated from the background with crisp edge definition, soft realistic shadow, and visible premium texture such as fabric weave, skin detail, leather grain, glass reflection, metal sheen, or product surface finish where appropriate.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]

4) Material accents: support the hero with surfaces implied by {브랜드 톤·시그니처}, such as linen folds, ceramic curvature, pale wood edges, stone slab texture, glass highlights, or woven fiber detail.

[1. PURPOSE]
Costco-inspired warehouse retail poster, bulk-value promotional catalog look, vertical advertising layout for product or store showcase.
Create a visually unmistakable warehouse-membership retail aesthetic with oversized pricing, stacked product abundance, pallet displays, aisle signage, barcode/coupon details, and practical value-forward energy.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center composition: {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} occupies the lower 55% as the primary hero, with a strong frontal perspective, stacked bulk inventory around it, and dense but readable retail framing.
- Header zone: upper 18% contains a bold warehouse flyer masthead, date label, issue number, and main callout text in Korean, with a price hierarchy that feels like an in-store promo board.
- Background treatment: bright warehouse interior feel with white ceiling panels, exposed industrial beams, gray concrete floor, metal racks, stacked cartons, pallet edges, aisle markers, shopping carts, and wide aisle depth fading into the distance.
- Signage and labels: large price blocks, member-value callouts, barcode/coupon area, SKU lines, quantity tags, and small secondary info cards arranged in a stacked retail grid with hard-edged rectangular panels.
- Add realistic retail details: shelf labels, yellow/white price cards, warehouse bay numbers, sample counter sign, membership card graphic, small footer disclaimer, address/contact line, and a tiny print-production code.
- Use {브랜드 톤·시그니처}, {컬러 팔레트}, {라이팅·무드}, {타이포·카피}, {레이아웃}, {비율} to keep the visual language consistent.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background layer: render a full warehouse-store environment with bright overhead LED panels, long aisle perspective, tall steel shelving, palletized bulk packages, cardboard box texture, concrete floor scuffs, and practical retail signage that suggests wholesale scale.
2. Hero layer: place {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} as the dominant focal object, slightly below center, with crisp commercial-product-photo presence, realistic reflections, shelf context, and nearby stacked inventory for abundance.
3. Header architecture: build a top flyer band with Korean text such as "창고형 특가", "VOL.247", "2026년 5월호", "이번 주 회원 전용", plus a small date range label "05.01–05.31" and a narrow vertical spine/credit text reading "WAREHOUSE VALUE GUIDE".
4. Price architecture: add oversized bold price signage near the hero, using blocky rectangular tags, strong hierarchy, compact supporting text, and Korean price copy such as "회원가", "큰 가격", "₩7,500 할인", "1박스 기준", "LIMIT 2".
5. Supporting labels: place smaller information modules around the hero—product facts, quantity cues, value highlights, SKU number, item code, unit price, barcode area, QR-style coupon box, and shelf-card captions—aligned like a busy big-box wholesale circular.
6. Promotional modules: include 2-3 short Korean feature blurbs such as "벌크로 더 크게", "가성비 장보기", "주말 한정 쿠폰", and a footer strip with "매장별 재고 상이 · 자세한 내용은 고객센터 문의".
7. Brand-tone translation: express {브랜드 톤·시그니처} through bulk packaging emphasis, practical abundance, large warehouse signs, member-deal messaging, and retail-operational realism.
8. Color control: apply {컬러 팔레트} across signage, price blocks, cart handles, divider strips, and accent areas, while using neutral grays, cardboard browns, metallic shelving, and floor texture to support the red/white/black retail system.
9. Final polish: add realistic print/promo finish with sharp panel edges, light paper grain, subtle ink density variation, small registration marks, barcode texture, and polished retail-catalog clarity.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold condensed sans-serif for prices and headers, with Korean support in Pretendard or Noto Sans KR; title weight 800-900, price numerals oversized, supporting text 400-600, microcopy still legible.
- Korean copy examples to render inside the design: "창고형 특가", "회원가", "큰 가격", "벌크", "가성비", "이번 주 추천", "대용량 기획", "재고 소진 시 종료".
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트} anchored by vivid retail red, pure white, and deep black; use neutral grays for warehouse structure, cardboard kraft tones for boxes, yellow shelf-card accents, and metallic rack highlights.
- Border/shadow: crisp rectangular panels, utilitarian dividers, price-card outlines, shelf-tag borders, subtle 2-4px drop shadow, 10-14px blur, 12-18% opacity, like real printed signage mounted in a warehouse aisle.
- Layout discipline: use hard alignment, large price emphasis, stacked modular information, barcode/footer details, and dense retail flyer rhythm like a big-box wholesale catalog page or in-store promotional poster.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: wide 24mm lens, eye-level slightly low angle, f/5.6, realistic commercial retail photography framing with strong depth cues.
- Lighting: overhead warehouse LED panels mixed with soft daylight spill from high side windows, even exposure, bright practical reflections on packaging, visible highlights on plastic wrap, metal racks, and polished product surfaces.
- Color grade: high-contrast retail grade with clean whites, saturated red accents, neutral concrete grays, cardboard browns, and controlled black shadows.
- Realism cues: include slight floor scuffs, pallet wood grain, plastic shrink-wrap shine, small price-ticket perforations, carton seams, tape lines, shelf rail labels, and realistic perspective on all signs.

[6. MOOD]
Big-box wholesale editorial — a Costco circular meets warehouse retail poster, with the efficient, value-forward look of a modern supermarket ad spread, full of pallet-scale abundance, bright aisle lighting, practical signage, and believable promotional detail.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render these strings exactly as written, if they appear in the layout: "회원가", "큰 가격", "벌크", "가성비".
- Include realistic Korean retail microcopy such as "창고형 특가", "2026년 5월호", "VOL.247", "05.01–05.31", "재고 소진 시 종료", "매장별 재고 상이" when space allows.
- Preserve warehouse-retail hierarchy: the hero subject, oversized price block, header masthead, coupon/barcode area, and smaller support info must remain clearly separated and readable.
- Keep {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} as the main subject and preserve {브랜드 톤·시그니처}, {컬러 팔레트}, {라이팅·무드}, {타이포·카피}, {레이아웃}, {비율} in the visual execution.

[4. STYLE RULES]

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero area (mid 55%): {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} rendered as the primary visual focus, shot as a crisp commercial subject with crunchy fried texture, warm oil sheen, visible seasoning specks, clean edge separation, and a slightly elevated angle. Add natural companion elements where appropriate, such as a red paper bucket, fries sleeve, biscuit, sauce cup, branded paper liner, napkin corner, a few realistic crumbs, and condensation on a drink cup, without overpowering the hero.
2. Supporting color blocks: bold red and white panels frame the subject, with warm brown and golden accents reinforcing the Kentucky fast-food mood. Include diagonal stripe panels, small checkerboard diner accents, subtle paper grain, and a golden burst shape behind the hero for promotional energy.
3. Headline zone (upper 15%): {타이포·카피} placed in a large advertisement-style arrangement with strong hierarchy, wide tracking for the main line, and a compact subtitle beneath. Add short Korean promo copy such as “오늘의 켄터키 크런치”, “바삭함이 터지는 순간”, and a small line “NEW WEEKLY SPECIAL” as secondary type.

Include realistic menu information: “SET ₩7,500”, “치킨 2조각 + 비스킷 + 콜라”, “런치 한정 11:00–14:00”, “매장 픽업 가능”, and a small coupon/QR-style box labeled “쿠폰 코드: CRUNCH247”.

Add a narrow vertical side text strip reading “KENTUCKY STYLE CRISPY CHICKEN” for a believable printed-ad finish.
6. Texture and finish: subtle fried-food gloss, paper-print poster texture, laminated menu-board sheen, warm reflections on sauce, soft shadow under packaging, and polished studio cutout treatment so the image looks like a premium fast-food campaign board rather than a flat mockup.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold sans-serif display fonts such as Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for Korean, paired with a compact condensed English style; headline size large, subtitle medium, supporting info small. Use realistic hierarchy with price numerals oversized, coupon text tiny but sharp, and feature blurbs arranged like a finished QSR retail poster.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트} with dominant #C8102E red, clean white #FFFFFF, warm brown #6B3F2A, and golden yellow #D9A441. Allow deep fryer-gold highlights, toasted shadows, creamy paper whites, and small black type accents for menu readability.
- Border/shadow: use a soft but defined drop shadow under the hero subject, around 4px vertical offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity, plus thin clean separators for copy blocks. Add subtle die-cut label shapes, coupon boxes, small barcode framing, and printed divider rules to create a realistic promotional layout.

- Brand tone: {브랜드 톤·시그니처} should feel like a confident Kentucky fast-food campaign, with energetic retail graphics, strong red-white-gold contrast, and appetizing commercial polish.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio commercial food photography with a 90mm macro lens at f/8, sharp subject detail, shallow but controlled depth separation, and clean perspective.
- Lighting: studio key light from upper-left at 45° with a warm golden fill from the right, plus subtle rim light to define edges and texture. Reflect {라이팅·무드} through warm highlights on the food, gentle gloss on packaging, and controlled specular shine on sauce and drink surfaces.

- Rendering quality: high-resolution commercial print finish, crisp Korean typography, realistic menu-board material, lightly textured paper background, and detailed product photography suitable for a premium restaurant promotion.

Fast-food campaign poster — bold Kentucky diner advertising energy with a polished commercial menu-board feel, like a premium QSR key visual. The mood should feel appetizing, loud, warm, and retail-ready, with believable in-store promotional information and a sense of fresh hot food just served.

- Composition must remain a vertical commercial poster with a strong hero-first hierarchy, not a casual lifestyle scene.

North Face-inspired mountain brand visual for advertising, poster, or catalog use. Extreme outdoor editorial aesthetic with dramatic alpine scale, built to feel like a premium expedition campaign with a believable real-world print-poster finish.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} placed as the visual anchor, with mountain terrain, weather energy, expedition equipment details, and campaign information supporting the story.

- Poster information layer: integrate a bold campaign headline area, short Korean subcopy, date/location line, route or altitude label, small product/field-test spec notes, tiny credit line, and a barcode or QR-style catalog area so it feels like a real premium outdoor advertisement.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero landscape layer: build a vast alpine scene with steep ridgelines, high-contrast rock faces, snow-loaded ledges, visible wind trails, and atmospheric depth so the environment feels dominant and extreme.
- Subject integration: place {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} in a believable outdoor position, with accurate scale, natural contact shadows, snow interaction, wet fabric sheen, dust, frost, or trail debris matching the mountain environment.

- Real poster details: add small text blocks like 'EXPEDITION REPORT VOL.247', '2026.05.18 강원 설악 루트', 'FIELD NOTE 04', 'MODEL CREDIT: KIM DOYUN', 'PHOTO: ALPINE CREW', plus a barcode/QR-style rectangle and compact product tag area near an edge.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use bold sans-serif Korean/English pairing such as Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for main text, with compact tracking and strong uppercase-like structure for English accents.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} with deep charcoal #111111, TNF-style red #D71920, alpine green #2F5D50, and clean off-white #F5F5F1 as dominant anchors.

- Border/shadow: subtle hard-edged editorial shadow, 20% opacity, light blur only where physically plausible; if framing is used, make it utilitarian like a high-end outdoor catalog layout with small crop marks, section labels, and printed texture.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame 24mm wide-angle at f/5.6 for landscape dominance, or 35mm f/4 if the subject needs slightly tighter campaign framing.
- Lighting: overcast diffused mountain daylight with a strong side key from camera-left, plus faint rim separation from the sky; follow {라이팅·무드} and add storm-window contrast, snow glare, or cold reflected light for drama.
- Color grade: deep charcoal shadows, cold stone grays, restrained natural greens, and saturated expedition red accents with crisp highlight roll-off.

[6. MOOD]
Premium alpine expedition campaign — like a Patagonia / Arc'teryx / National Geographic adventure editorial with a high-end outdoor brand poster sensibility, intense mountain weather, practical gear realism, and confident performance-driven storytelling.

- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

7. Footer / info strip: anchor a thin bottom information area with tiny caption text, date-like details, page/catalog number, small divider rules, and micro-print credits; make it feel printed and tactile while the collage remains dominant.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a hand-drawn script-like headline feel combined with Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the Korean subcopy, and a condensed vintage sans-serif for supporting text; headline 54–72px feel, subcopy 22–28px feel, micro credits 8–12px feel.
- Korean copy rendering: set bold poster lines in Korean, including “나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답”, “거리에서 시작된 새 시즌”, and “오늘만 열리는 드롭”, with proper Hangul spacing and clean letterforms.
- Color palette: vintage beige, muted red, deep green, mustard yellow, with off-black text and slightly washed highlights; keep saturation aged rather than bright, using {컬러 팔레트} as the controlling reference.
- Border/shadow: thin paper-edge borders, uneven torn edges, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity, plus subtle print wear, ink bleed, misregistration, creased corners, and tape gloss.
- Layout density: make the poster feel content-rich and real, with layered ephemera, readable headline hierarchy, practical event information, and tactile street-wall details rather than a sterile mockup.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm documentary street-photo look, shot as if on a Canon AE-1 or Nikon F3 with a 35mm f/2 lens, slightly imperfect framing and analog grain.
- Lighting: {라이팅·무드}, warm late-afternoon ambient light with mild directional side light from upper-left, plus soft fill to preserve detail in the collage layers.
- Color grade: faded film stock grade with amber highlights, beige midtones, muted olive shadows, and slight red-channel lift for an old poster print feel.
- Material realism: visible matte paper texture, real tape reflections, uneven pasted layers, scratched ink, staple holes, subtle dust, folded flyer marks, and natural shadows between paper pieces.

[6. MOOD]
Vintage skate-zine editorial — raw photocopied street poster energy with a 90s magazine spread attitude, handmade collage roughness, and the feeling of a real local drop announcement found on a city wall.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: no broken Hangul characters anywhere in the image.
- The visual identity must strongly evoke Stussy-like vintage street culture through collage composition, aged paper, handwritten typography energy, and skate-street editorial rhythm.
- If any Korean text appears, it must render cleanly and legibly with proper spacing and no character corruption.
- Include realistic Korean poster information such as “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “스트리트 샘플 세일”, “성수 창고 3층”, “2026.05.24 토”, “오후 2시–9시”, “입장 ₩7,000”, and “문의 @street_archive”.
- Keep {비율} reflected in the visual balance and subject scale while preserving the vertical 1024x1536 poster format.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Patagonia-inspired outdoor editorial poster / catalog visual that sells a rugged natural-active lifestyle without using the actual logo. Vertical ad composition for brand campaigns, social posts, or product storytelling.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} becomes the hero, occupying roughly 55–65% of the frame, with the visual weight anchored slightly below center for a grounded, mountain-ad feel.
- Background treatment: layered mountain ridges, wind-shaped clouds, stone textures, and open sky; keep the scene expansive, with no busy urban elements.
- Framing and spacing: leave breathable negative space in the upper third for headline copy; keep the lower area textured and tactile, with clean edge separation between subject and background.
- Brand tone application: translate {브랜드 톤·시그니처} into a credible alpine/outdoor editorial language rather than a literal logo treatment.
- Palette usage: build the scene around {컬러 팔레트}, using natural contrast between earth tones and crisp whites, with a restrained red accent for energy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background base: establish a dramatic mountain-and-sky environment with atmospheric depth, using layered silhouettes and slightly desaturated distance haze.
2. Hero block: place {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} as the focal anchor, rendered with strong material clarity and a believable outdoor context.
3. Color integration: distribute {컬러 팔레트} so green and brown tones live in terrain and clothing/material surfaces, white in sky highlights or negative space, charcoal in shadows, and red only as a controlled accent.
4. Motion / active energy: suggest wind, stride, fabric pull, dust, or weather tension to reinforce the active lifestyle feel while keeping the frame editorial and composed.
5. Typography zone: reserve a clean copy area for {타이포·카피}, using bold stacked type above or beside the hero with clear hierarchy and generous breathing room.
6. Layout discipline: keep {레이아웃} as a decisive structure — strong central subject, landscape pressure in the background, and poster-like balance that feels campaign-ready.
7. Format fidelity: maintain the vertical {비율} framing with enough top and side margin for a premium print-ad look.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use bold sans-serif Korean/Latin pairing such as Pretendard Bold, Noto Sans KR SemiBold, or Akzidenz-style grotesk; headline 48–72px equivalent, subtitle 22–30px equivalent, with tight but readable line spacing.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트} mapped into concrete tones like grass green #4F6B4A, natural brown #7A5A3A, off-white #F4F1EA, charcoal #2A2A2A, and accent red #C0392B.
- Border/shadow: minimal or none; if needed, use a soft natural shadow under the subject, about 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity, to keep the cutout grounded.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: medium-format outdoor editorial look, e.g. Hasselblad X2D with 90mm lens at f/5.6 for crisp subject detail and compressed mountain layers, or a 35mm lens at f/8 for a broader campaign frame.
- Lighting: overcast diffused daylight with a subtle directional break from upper-left, plus gentle rim light from the sky edge to define contours; preserve realistic cloud softness and weather texture.
- Color grade: Patagonia-style outdoor grade with earthy greens, muted browns, cool slate shadows, clean whites, and a restrained warm-red accent; slight matte contrast, no oversaturation.

[6. MOOD]
Premium outdoor brand editorial — National Geographic adventure spread meets a modern Patagonia campaign aesthetic, with rugged authenticity and disciplined composition.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered image must correctly show these verbatim Korean strings if included: "브랜드 톤·시그니처", "적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)", "컬러 팔레트", "라이팅·무드", "타이포·카피", "레이아웃", "비율".
- Do not include the actual Patagonia logo.
- Keep the image unmistakably outdoor, natural, and active; avoid urban, luxury-fashion, or studio-only styling.
- Korean characters must render cleanly with no broken glyphs.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Sexualized posing or exposure emphasis
- Overblown advertising copy
- Urban/sci-fi/neon styling that breaks the outdoor editorial identity

[1. PURPOSE]
Advertising poster / catalog visual that captures the iconic red-box streetwear brand language as a realistic fashion drop key visual. Make it feel like a printed streetwear campaign poster photographed for an editorial catalog: bold red block identity, real product or model presence, credible event information, retail details, and sharp Korean promotional typography.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} placed as the central hero, occupying about 55–65% of the frame, with a strong poster-like presence and believable physical detail such as fabric weave, product edges, store fixtures, skin texture, tags, seams, or packaging surfaces when appropriate.
- Brand tone: {브랜드 톤·시그니처} expressed through a large red rectangular brand block, bold streetwear typography, drop-announcement cues, and disciplined graphic hierarchy.
- Background treatment: studio-white or near-white printed-paper backdrop with realistic matte poster grain, faint paper fibers, light handling marks, and subtle contact shadows that make the layout feel physically printed and photographed.
- Framing direction: vertical editorial poster layout, centered hierarchy, crisp red-box anchor, catalog-style crop marks, small production credits, and balanced top/bottom information zones.
- Palette usage: keep {컬러 팔레트} dominant, with vivid red as the primary visual anchor, white as the clean poster field, and black reserved for headline, labels, captions, small ticket text, barcode marks, and fine outlines.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero area (mid 60%): {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)} presented directly with a polished studio catalog look, centered or slightly lower-center; include natural details such as garment folds, matte plastic packaging, product label texture, shoe sole marks, store counter reflections, or realistic portrait lighting depending on the subject.
2. Brand block area: a bold red rectangle or panel integrated into the composition as the signature visual anchor; keep it flat, graphic, ink-like, and print-based rather than glossy 3D. Inside or near it, place a fictional Korean/English drop title in bold type, not a copied official wordmark.
3. Copy area: {타이포·카피} placed in a compact stacked treatment aligned to the red block edges or bottom third. Add realistic short Korean poster copy such as “새 시즌 드롭”, “한정 발매”, “오늘의 실루엣”, or “거리에서 완성되는 태도”.
4. Event / retail detail band: include a credible poster information strip with Korean details: “DROP NO. 027”, “2026.05.18 SAT 12:00”, “성수 플래그십 / 온라인 동시 발매”, “입장권 ₩7,500”, “문의 @redbox.seoul”.
5. Catalog production details: add a small barcode area, tiny QR-like ticket block, page/catalog code such as “LOOKBOOK P.04”, model or product credit “MODEL: JIWON K.” / “ITEM: BOX FIT HOODIE”, and fine-print staff credit text along one edge.
6. Layout discipline: {레이아웃} should feel bold and editorial, with one dominant focal point, one primary red block, and several small realistic poster details that support the campaign without competing with the hero subject.
7. Size logic: {비율} with tall poster proportions, strong vertical reading order, and enough breathing room around the hero and red block for a premium streetwear catalog impression.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold condensed sans-serif such as Helvetica Neue Condensed, DIN Condensed, or Noto Sans KR Bold; headline size large and tight, subcopy smaller and controlled, with believable Korean typesetting and consistent baseline alignment.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트} with vivid brand red #D6001C, pure white #FFFFFF, and deep black #111111; use tiny gray registration marks or paper shadows only if they support the printed-poster realism.
- Graphic details: include crop marks, small barcode block, ticket-stub line, micro captions, date label, and sponsor/partner area rendered as simple text labels such as “STUDIO PARTNER”, “SEOUL DROP GUIDE”, “STYLE CREDIT”.
- Shadow / depth: use clean contact shadows under the product or person, slight paper curl or poster surface variation, and subtle soft drop shadow where needed to separate object from background.
- Print feel: clean matte poster finish, slightly compressed contrast, crisp text edges, realistic ink density, faint paper grain, and no metallic effects.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio product photography look, full-frame camera with 85mm f/1.8 or 70–200mm at 135mm, straight-on or slightly elevated angle for a polished catalog poster.
- Lighting: hard studio key light from upper-left at roughly 45°, controlled fill on the right, strong but clean shadow edges, with realistic specular control on fabric, skin, packaging, glass, or store fixtures.
- Color grade: high-contrast red / white / black grade, slightly cool neutrals with saturated brand red preserved, editorial fashion-ad look.
- Realism cues: preserve visible material texture, accurate shadows, natural garment drape, readable printed labels, slight poster paper grain, and believable physical scale between the hero subject and graphic elements.

[6. MOOD]
Iconic streetwear campaign poster — confrontational, premium, and instantly recognizable like a high-end fashion drop announcement photographed for a magazine spread, with retail-event credibility and bold Korean street-culture energy.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear exactly and clearly if shown: {브랜드 톤·시그니처}, {적용 대상 (제품·매장·인물 자유)}, {컬러 팔레트}, {라이팅·무드}, {타이포·카피}, {레이아웃}, {비율}.
- Render additional Korean poster text cleanly and legibly, for example: “새 시즌 드롭”, “한정 발매”, “2026.05.18 SAT 12:00”, “성수 플래그십”, “입장권 ₩7,500”, “문의 @redbox.seoul”.
- Keep the visual language red-box streetwear editorial, but make the image feel like a real printed campaign poster with believable product/model details, barcode area, ticket information, date label, credits, and matte paper texture.
- If a logo-like red rectangle is used, make it a fictional campaign block or typographic label rather than a distorted imitation wordmark.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness
