[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean supermarket promotional ad poster, vertical retail flyer for fresh groceries and household essentials.
Designed for a Homeplus-style in-store campaign with clear pricing, product emphasis, weekly-deal urgency, and family-shopping appeal.
Make it look like a real printed mart advertisement photographed or rendered with practical retail detail: product bundles, price tags, aisle context, coupon blocks, date labels, membership notes, and a credible mass-market flyer finish.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main hero area occupies the upper 52% of the frame, showing {제품·소재} arranged as the primary visual cluster with strong shelf-like retail clarity, abundant stacking, visible package faces, fresh produce texture, and small promotional tag cards tucked between items.
- Brand headline zone sits in the top 12% with {카피·타이포} set as the most readable element, accompanied by a small campaign label such as "전단행사 VOL.247", "2026년 5월 1주차", and "행사기간 05.01(금)–05.07(목)".
- Price and category modules fill the lower third in a grid-like retail layout, with {레이아웃} balanced for quick scanability and including multiple item cards, red discount badges, membership price notes, barcode area, coupon strip, and tiny store-information text.
- Background uses a realistic store-inspired surface with subtle aisle depth, refrigerated-case glow, shopping-cart handle glimpses, bright white base, and fresh green accents to support {브랜드 톤}.
- Compose with practical flyer density: readable blocks, overlapping sale stickers, receipt-like microcopy, shelf labels, small icons for delivery/pickup/member benefit, and tactile printed-paper shadows.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header strip (top 12%): Place the main Korean masthead in bold, highly legible retail typography, with {카피·타이포} centered and strong visual weight. Include supporting header details: "홈플러스", "이번 주 장보기 특가", "마이홈플러스 회원 혜택", "행사기간 2026.05.01–05.07", plus a small issue/date label on the right.
- Hero product block (upper-middle 40%): Showcase {제품·소재} as a fresh, abundant arrangement with a realistic supermarket display feel, including neat stacking, slight perspective depth, visible condensation on chilled items, produce stems and leaves, crinkled packaging, carton edges, and shelf-price tabs.
- Secondary category chips (mid-lower left/right): Add small retail category tags that echo {시그니처 결}, using compact boxes and clean alignment. Example Korean chips: "신선식품", "정육·수산", "간편식", "생활용품", "오늘의 특가", "1+1 모음".
- Price table area (lower 26%): Present pricing modules in a structured grid with large numerals, small Korean labels, and clear separation lines for immediate readability. Include realistic sample cards such as "제철 과일 모음 7,990원", "국내산 삼겹살 100g 1,980원", "우유 2입 5,980원", "라면 멀티팩 3,980원", "키친타월 6롤 6,900원", "마이홈플러스 회원가".
- Footer emphasis (bottom 10%): Use a concise brand-supporting strip that reinforces {브랜드 톤}. Add store and campaign utility details: "가까운 홈플러스에서 만나요", "온라인 주문 가능", "매장별 취급 상품 상이", "고객센터 1577-3355", a small barcode block, QR-style coupon square, address-line placeholder like "서울 강서구 화곡로 398 홈플러스", and tiny legal-style retail microcopy.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard and Noto Sans KR for the main Korean copy, bold 700–900 weight for headline, medium 500–600 for supporting text, price numbers at very large display size. Use compressed retail numerals for prices and smaller caption text for unit pricing and membership notes.
- Color palette: Homeplus signature red, pure white, fresh green, and neutral light gray; use exact-feeling tones like #D6001C, #FFFFFF, #2F8F4E, #F4F4F4. Add small yellow/orange sale accents for discount bursts and coupon highlights while keeping {컬러 팔레트} recognizable.
- Border/shadow: thin clean dividers, subtle 2px lines, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity on product cards. Add printed flyer textures, slight paper grain, tiny crop marks, glossy label highlights, and natural shadows under stacked products.
- Retail graphic detail: include red price flags, green freshness ribbons, small delivery/pickup icons, membership badge shapes, coupon perforation marks, barcode area, QR-like square, and store aisle signage elements integrated around the main offer.
- Copy style: Korean retail phrasing should feel believable and short, using text such as "놓치면 아쉬운 7일 특가", "오늘 장보기 끝", "신선함을 담은 가격", "회원 전용 혜택", and "한정 수량" without making unrealistic claims.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: commercial retail photography look, full-frame 35mm lens at f/5.6 for product clarity, slight overhead angle mixed with front-facing poster composition.
- Lighting: bright store ambient light with soft diffused overhead panels, mild amber fill from the front, controlled highlights on fresh produce and package edges, gentle reflections on plastic wrap and refrigerated product labels.
- Color grade: clean supermarket commercial grade with vivid red accents, neutral whites, saturated greens, and warm amber balance.
- Material realism: products should have natural imperfections, readable-ish packaging blocks, paper price labels, sticker edges, produce texture, condensation beads, folded flyer corners, and realistic shadow contact points.

[6. MOOD]
Mainstream Korean supermarket weekly-deal poster — practical, high-clarity retail advertising with the feel of a large chain flyer, in-store promotional signage, and a busy but readable family grocery campaign.
The mood is energetic, trustworthy, value-focused, and fresh, like a real mart entrance poster customers would stop to scan before shopping.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: "홈플러스", "이번 주 장보기 특가", "행사기간 2026.05.01–05.07", "마이홈플러스 회원가", 가격 정보, 카테고리 표기, 한글 부제.
- Include realistic visible Korean flyer details: "전단행사 VOL.247", "제철 과일", "정육·수산", "간편식", "생활용품", "온라인 주문 가능", "매장별 취급 상품 상이", and at least four large won prices such as "7,990원", "1,980원", "5,980원", "3,980원".
- Layout invariants: the composition must stay vertical, product hero must remain dominant in the upper half, and pricing modules must stay cleanly organized in the lower section.
- Preserve all placeholder-driven styling: {브랜드 톤}, {시그니처 결}, {제품·소재}, {무드·라이팅}, {컬러 팔레트}, {카피·타이포}, {레이아웃}, {비율}.
- Do not distort or stylize Korean characters into unreadable forms.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536
- title: 이마트 트레이더스 광고

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean warehouse-club supermarket advertisement poster, vertical retail promo with bold pricing hierarchy, abundant bulk-product merchandising, and realistic in-store flyer details.
Designed for in-store promotion, social feed ad, printed flyer, membership-event notice, and warehouse-club seasonal sale marketing.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main hero product cluster occupies the lower-middle 55% of the frame, with a large price block anchored according to {레이아웃}.
- Background should read as a believable Korean warehouse-store interior: bright ceiling LED grid, tall pallet racks, aisle-number signage, freezer-case glow, checkout-line hints, and shallow shopper movement in the far background.
- Use {브랜드톤} as the overall brand voice, while {시그니처결} guides visual density, bulk-pack scale, family-shopping energy, and value-focused retail confidence.
- Place {제품군} as stacked merchandising groups: front-facing bulk packs, beverage cartons, family-size snack boxes, instant noodle bundles, seasonal appliances, and folded apparel packs with visible price-card labels.
- Feature {대표상품} as the most readable front hero item, supported by secondary items in stepped layers so the poster feels like a real warehouse-club weekly deal wall.
- Add realistic promotional information: {행사명}, {행사기간}, {매장명}, {매장주소}, {문의전화}, {멤버십혜택}, QR-style coupon block, barcode strip, small item-code labels, and a bottom disclaimer line.
- The layout should feel like a real membership warehouse ad: big product, big price, bright sale badge, smaller supporting store information, and practical purchase cues all aligned with {레이아웃}.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 18%): set the main Korean retail title in a bold headline style. Include "이마트 트레이더스" or "트레이더스" with {행사명}, plus a small date ribbon showing {행사기간}.
2. Price hero zone (upper-mid 20%): place the largest price element as the focal point using {가격표기}, thick numerals, a red/yellow offer badge, and short labels such as "회원가", "대용량 특가", "이번 주 추천".
3. Product hero zone (middle 40%): show {제품군} as dense organized merchandising with {대표상품} in front, secondary product stacks behind, cart handles, pallet bases, shelf-edge tags, and readable package texture.
4. Store information zone (lower 15%): include {매장명}, {매장주소}, {문의전화}, operating-hours style text, parking/freezer pickup icons, and a small QR coupon tile with a barcode-like strip.
5. Membership benefit zone: add {멤버십혜택} in a compact badge or coupon card, plus small Korean microcopy such as "앱 쿠폰 확인", "재고 소진 시 종료", "일부 점포 제외".
6. Signature atmosphere: reinforce {시그니처결} with oversized retail scale, bulk-pack abundance, cart-friendly family shopping, practical savings, and lively Korean mart energy.
7. Background structure: add warehouse aisle depth, pallet shelving, overhead category signage, hanging price placards, and softly visible shoppers so the advertisement feels photographed in a real retail environment.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the headline, with a condensed sans for price details; title must read at thumbnail size and price digits should be the largest text on the poster.
- Color palette: {컬러팔레트} should dominate, with energetic yellow-red contrast, crisp white information panels, charcoal product labels, and high-visibility sale stickers.
- Border/shadow: use crisp retail cutout edges with a soft drop shadow of 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; price tags can use solid blocks, angled stickers, coupon tabs, and shelf-card dividers.
- Text treatment: {카피타이포} should appear as clear Korean typography with strong hierarchy: headline, event name, price, benefit badge, product callouts, store details, and fine-print disclaimer.
- Retail detail layer: include small but believable SKU numbers, unit-price marks, limited-quantity tags, QR coupon square, barcode strip, aisle signs, and category tabs to make the poster feel commercially produced.
- Product realism: packaging should have varied paper, plastic, cardboard, foil, and glossy beverage textures; keep readable front labels and believable reflections from overhead store lighting.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: realistic commercial product photography look, shot on a full-frame camera with a 35mm lens at f/8 for deep product clarity and store-scene context.
- Lighting: bright overhead store LED ambience mixed with soft daylight spill from one side, similar to a real supermarket promotional shoot; add gentle fill to keep packaging, price tags, and Korean type readable.
- Color grade: vivid retail commercial grade with clean whites, saturated yellow-red accents, appetizing product colors, and slightly cool neutral shadows to preserve the warehouse feel.
- Print finish: simulate a premium glossy flyer/poster surface with sharp ink edges, slight paper sheen, and realistic compression-free social-ad clarity.

[6. MOOD]
High-energy Korean warehouse-club retail promo — like a real grocery circular, in-store weekly sale poster, and social feed ad combined, with practical mass-market confidence, family-scale abundance, and immediate value appeal.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: "트레이더스", "{행사명}", "{행사기간}", "{가격표기}", "{매장명}"
- Korean text accuracy: 가격/부제/매장 정보/혜택 문구/상품 라벨의 모든 한글은 깨짐 없이 선명하게 렌더링.
- Required rendered Korean promo text examples: "회원가", "대용량 특가", "앱 쿠폰 확인", "재고 소진 시 종료", "일부 점포 제외".
- Layout invariant: large product hero + large price + event title + store information + coupon/barcode area must remain clearly separated and readable.
- Composition invariant: maintain the warehouse-club advertising feel with abundant merchandise, strong retail hierarchy, realistic product packaging, and believable Korean mart signage.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / government-style certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Fake celebrity composites or unauthorized public-figure likeness
- Deformed hands, faces, or shopper silhouettes

studio:prompts3:ours-726.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Costco-style warehouse club advertisement poster, tall vertical retail promo for bulk goods, membership pricing, and limited-time warehouse deals.
Commercial ad layout that feels like a real big-box weekly flyer photographed inside a busy warehouse store: stacked pallets, aisle signage, price cards, coupon-style information, and strong instant price hierarchy.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Top hero zone takes about 42% of the frame: {제품·소재} presented as the main commercial subject, arranged with bold scale contrast, visible bulk packaging, palletized quantity, shrink-wrap edges, shelf labels, and clear product mass.
- Mid-zone pricing area takes about 20%: oversized sale copy and membership price block placed immediately below the hero for fast scanning, with a coupon-card feel, SKU line, savings note, and short Korean promo phrase.
- Lower zone takes about 24%: warehouse interior cues, stacked pallets, aisle depth, checkout/member desk hints, store information panels, additional small deal tiles, and membership-service copy to reinforce the big-box retail setting.
- Background treatment: bright warehouse ceiling, visible metal beams, hanging aisle number signs, pallet stacks, concrete floor reflections, shopping cart silhouettes, yellow safety bollards, and realistic retail signage surfaces.
- Maintain strong left-to-right reading flow with layered retail details around the hero and price block: shelf talkers, small product labels, coupon strips, barcode/QR-style area, date label, and fine-print legal line.
- Use {브랜드 톤}, {시그니처 결}, and {레이아웃} as the core customizable structure while preserving the warehouse-club advertisement format.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero product block: place {제품·소재} in the upper-center with oversized scale, crisp edges, and a store-floor realism look; if multiple items appear, group them like a bulk-endcap display with visible packaging volume, repeated units, carton seams, pallet wood texture, shrink-wrap highlights, and retail shelf tags.
2. Price emphasis block: position {카피·타이포} directly beneath the hero in a dominant hierarchy, using a large bold price figure and smaller membership note beneath it, as if printed for a warehouse weekly flyer. Add supporting Korean microcopy such as "이번 주 창고특가", "온라인·매장 동시", "1인 2개 한정", "SKU 582-247" where it fits naturally.
3. Brand cue block: integrate {브랜드 톤} near the upper-left or upper-right as a strong retail identity anchor, with a flyer header line such as "WAREHOUSE SAVINGS", "VOL.247", "2026년 5월 1주", and a small member-service strip.
4. Signature retail texture: render {시그니처 결} through stacked cartons, pallet shrink-wrap, warehouse shelving depth, wide aisle perspective, price-tag rails, hanging category signs, floor reflections, and practical in-store materials.
5. Mood and lighting layer: apply {무드·라이팅} across the entire scene so the store feels bright, practical, high-traffic, and commercially real, with clear visibility on product surfaces, packaging nutrition/label blocks, price signage, and carton texture.
6. Color system: apply {컬러 팔레트} across headers, sale tags, coupon bands, member-price panels, aisle signs, and small informational badges; red pricing elements should stand out instantly against white, black, gray, and warehouse-neutral surfaces.
7. Layout anchor: follow {레이아웃} exactly, ensuring the top hero, central price, and bottom store/member information remain in clear stacked order while adding realistic flyer details such as store hours, date validity, barcode area, contact line, and secondary deal blurbs.
8. Format lock: keep {비율} as the final framing standard, with fully legible Korean typography, intact price figures, realistic product geometry, and preserved warehouse depth.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold condensed sans-serif for headline pricing, resembling Helvetica Neue Condensed Bold or Pretendard ExtraBold; price size should be the largest text on the poster, with smaller supporting copy in Noto Sans KR Medium. Use compact flyer typography for SKU, date, and fine print.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트} should be expressed with Costco-like red #E31837, white #FFFFFF, and black #111111, with cool gray warehouse neutrals, steel shelving, beige cardboard, yellow safety accents, and subtle blue membership-strip accents.
- Retail graphic details: include a top red header bar, membership-price card, small barcode/QR-style box, coupon clipping line, "기간 2026.05.01–05.07", "전국 창고형 매장", "오전 10시–오후 10시", and two or three short feature blurbs in Korean such as "대용량으로 더 알뜰하게", "회원 전용 즉시할인", "주말 장보기 추천".
- Border/shadow: use realistic print-ad panel shadows under product stacks and text panels, about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, with rectangular price blocks, thin divider rules, and small red corner tabs.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm full-frame documentary retail shot, f/5.6, eye-level to slightly low angle for a warehouse-endcap perspective, with enough depth to show aisle structure.
- Lighting: bright overhead LED warehouse lighting combined with daylight spill from storefront openings, slight cool fill from the left, crisp visibility on packaging edges, price cards, pallet wrap, and floor reflections.
- Color grade: high-contrast commercial retail grade with vivid red accents, neutral whites, steel-gray shelving, beige cardboard texture, yellow safety details, and clean black typography.

[6. MOOD]
High-volume warehouse club flyer — practical big-box retail editorial with the straightforward punch of Costco weekly promo design, enriched with real store atmosphere, member-only urgency, stacked inventory abundance, and believable weekly-sale information.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: "Costco", "KRW 39,900", "회원가".
- Additional Korean flyer text should be sharp and readable where present: "이번 주 창고특가", "기간 2026.05.01–05.07", "전국 창고형 매장", "대용량으로 더 알뜰하게", "회원 전용 즉시할인".
- Layout invariant: keep the vertical hierarchy of top hero product, central oversized price, and bottom store/member information.
- Typography invariant: the price must be the most visually dominant text element on the poster.

- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]

- Campaign footer: Add {캠페인 기간}, {매장 정보}, and {CTA} along the bottom in a refined retail footer, with a small QR-code-like square, channel handle "@hmhome.kr", and micro icons for online shop, store pickup, and gift wrapping.
- Accent details: Introduce {장식 요소} through seasonal color blocks, a small ribbon tag, a folded textile corner, a paper hangtag, and decorative graphic lines or dots that echo {컬러 팔레트} without overpowering the hero objects.
- Framing direction: Keep the image front-facing and stable, with slight editorial asymmetry in prop placement so the composition feels styled, lived-in, and realistic rather than flat.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold or Noto Sans KR Bold for the main brand line, with Pretendard Regular or Medium for Korean product captions and campaign details; main title around 72-96 px equivalent, secondary text around 24-36 px equivalent, product captions around 18-24 px equivalent, crisp anti-aliased edges.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

- Lighting: natural window light from upper-left at about 45°, softly diffused through sheer curtain, with a gentle fill from front-right and a faint warm practical bounce to support {분위기·라이팅}.

[6. MOOD]
Premium home decor editorial — a polished fashion retail campaign aesthetic with the calm, curated sensibility of Kinfolk x H&M Home styled set photography, enriched by realistic retail poster information, product prices, hangtags, and seasonal campaign details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered image must correctly include the fixed text string "H&M HOME" plus the Korean campaign copy from {메인 카피}, {컬렉션명}, {가격 라인}, {캠페인 기간}, {매장 정보}, and {CTA}.
- Required visible retail details: include 2-3 readable item price captions, a small QR-code-like square, the handle "@hmhome.kr", and the spine credit "HOME EDIT / SEOUL / VOL.247".
- Layout invariants: maintain a front-facing hero composition, clearly readable brand hierarchy, realistic product scale, tactile homeware materials, and an editorial retail footer.
- Keep all objects realistic, well-proportioned, and sharply styled; products must look like home decor items rather than abstract shapes.

[1. PURPOSE]
Luxury interior advertising poster in the Zara Home style, designed as an editorial product-led brand image for social media, boutique display, and print-like campaign use. Focus on a refined home-lifestyle composition with premium catalog polish, realistic product information, and believable retail poster details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: a large still-life hero arrangement of {제품·소재} occupying the lower 62% of the frame, with the visual anchor slightly below center for a balanced luxury advertising spread feel.
- Brand tone: express {브랜드 톤} through refined spacing, soft contrast, tactile surfaces, and curated home styling.
- Signature texture: build the scene around {시그니처 결} with visible linen weave, matte ceramic pores, pale wood grain, wax texture, folded fabric edges, and small paper product tags.
- Background treatment: shallow-focus interior backdrop with blurred architectural lines, soft window glow, a warm neutral wall, a stone tabletop, and gentle bokeh that feels like a premium home showroom set.
- Poster information layer: place the masthead “ZARA HOME” at the top, followed by “NEW SEASON LIVING”, {한글 부제}, {시즌·날짜}, and a small campaign note so the poster reads as a real seasonal interior advertisement.
- Retail detail layer: integrate {가격 정보}, {스토어 정보}, {웹사이트}, {행사 정보}, {스폰서 문구}, and {하단 CTA} as small refined footer text, product tag text, or side-label information.
- Framing: vertical 1024x1536 poster layout with an elegant upper title band, a detailed product scene in the lower field, and a footer area containing store, event, and contact information.
- Text placement: keep the main typography aligned with the product geometry, using thin divider lines, small material labels, and a discreet square QR-style mark near the footer.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background plane — Create a softly lit neutral interior base in beige, warm stone, or off-white, with subtle wall plaster texture, a stone or pale wood surface, and blurred showroom depth.
2. Hero still life — Place {제품·소재} as a refined layered composition, mixing one dominant object with several supporting pieces, folded linens, stacked towels, a ceramic vessel, a candle, and a small product card.
3. Material contrast — Emphasize the contrast between linen softness, ceramic matte surfaces, wax translucency, and wood warmth, with realistic fibers, edges, creases, grain, and contact shadows.
4. Light shaping — Use {무드·라이팅} so the edges of the objects fall into soft shadow while the highlights remain gentle, premium, and photographic rather than glossy.
5. Main copy block — Set “ZARA HOME” large in the upper area, “NEW SEASON LIVING” beneath it, then {한글 부제} and {시즌·날짜} in smaller Korean editorial type.
6. Information block — Add a believable poster footer: {행사 정보}, {스토어 정보}, {웹사이트}, {가격 정보}, and {스폰서 문구}, separated by fine hairline rules and small typographic dividers.
7. Decorative graphics — Add subtle catalog-style accents such as thin vertical rules, tiny material swatch labels, a small page-code like “HOME EDIT 05”, and a discreet QR-style square, all integrated into the luxury layout.
8. Layout balance — Keep {레이아웃} with the background blur strongest behind the upper copy and the clearest focus on the central product grouping.
9. Color discipline — Apply {컬러 팔레트} consistently across products, textiles, wall tones, tabletop, paper tags, and accent objects so the whole poster reads as one coherent luxury palette.
10. Final polish — Ensure the entire image feels like a high-end lifestyle catalog advertisement: carefully styled, tactile, commercially believable, and ready for a seasonal home collection campaign.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean, paired with a clean modern sans-serif for English; masthead weight 700–800, subtitle weight 300–400, footer weight 300–500, headline size large with wide tracking.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트}, with muted beige foundations, charcoal anchor notes, warm cream paper labels, and one controlled accent such as terracotta or sage.
- Layout system: editorial grid with a top masthead, centered product hero, left or right micro-labels, and a bottom information strip containing date, venue, store, price, and web details.
- Graphic details: include fine divider lines, small catalog numbers, material tags, a discreet QR-style mark, and soft natural drop shadows under objects, about 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity, plus subtle ambient occlusion at contact points.
- Copy hierarchy: “ZARA HOME” must feel like the primary brand mark; “NEW SEASON LIVING” and {한글 부제} should feel editorial; store, price, and event information should be readable but secondary.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame editorial product photography look, 50mm lens at f/2.8 for gentle depth separation, or 85mm f/4 for a tighter luxury catalog perspective.
- Lighting: soft natural side light from upper-left at roughly 45°, with mild bounce fill from the right and diffuse falloff across the background.
- Color grade: warm cream, beige, charcoal, and muted sage/terracotta grading with low saturation, slightly lifted blacks, and a polished magazine finish.
- Surface realism: show linen fibers, ceramic pores, wood grain, candle wax edges, paper tag texture, folded towel thickness, and delicate shadows where objects overlap.

[6. MOOD]
Premium interior editorial — like a Zara Home / Kinfolk / The Gentlewoman home spread with calm luxury, tactile material emphasis, seasonal retail storytelling, and quiet boutique sophistication.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered image must preserve these strings exactly as written: “ZARA HOME”, “NEW SEASON LIVING”, “린넨과 세라믹으로 완성한 조용한 집”, “2026년 5월 컬렉션”, “런칭 프리뷰 2026.05.18 11:00–20:00”, “zara.com/home”.
- Composition invariant: keep a large hero still life with soft bokeh background, an upper brand-and-collection title area, and a believable lower poster footer with store, price, event, sponsor, and contact information.
- Visual fidelity: maintain natural material texture, refined home styling, premium catalog lighting, and a calm high-end retail advertisement feel.
- Realism requirement: all printed elements should look physically plausible on a luxury poster or catalog ad, with legible Korean microcopy, stable alignment, and no warped typography.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications / government-like endorsement marks
- Broken Korean characters or unreadable Hangul
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public-figure likenesses

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean furniture brand advertising poster for a Hanssem-inspired home interior campaign, vertical 1024x1536 retail poster for family/lifestyle promotion.
Commercial editorial composition that sells a full-room furniture story with premium retail polish, warm domestic realism, and believable in-store promotional information.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall framing: tall 1024x1536 poster, top hero zone 32%, center product showcase 38%, lower promotion/information zone 22%, footer disclaimer strip 8%, designed like a real Korean furniture brand campaign displayed in a showroom, elevator screen, or mall lightbox.
- Main subject placement: {시그니처 결} arranged as the visual anchor across the hero and mid sections, with {제품·소재} layered in a real Korean apartment setting and a relaxed family presence guided by {브랜드 톤}.
- Background treatment: Korean new-wedding apartment interior with off-white plaster walls, light oak flooring, linen curtains, a small side table with a ceramic mug, framed family photo, folded throw blanket, indoor plant, fabric texture on cushions, and subtle daylight bounce.
- Spacing and framing: retail-ad hierarchy with clear left-to-right reading flow, readable copy blocks, product callout tags, believable furniture proportions, and enough visible lifestyle details to make the home feel lived-in and purchasable.
- Use {브랜드 톤} and {레이아웃} as the organizing logic for the entire layout, while keeping the poster visually premium and sales-oriented.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero area (top 32%): a warm Korean family-home scene in the style of a premium furniture catalog, showing a parent couple and child naturally interacting near the sofa or dining table; keep the camera slightly wide so the room feels spacious and architecturally plausible.
2. Brand and campaign headline: place the brand wordmark area and main copy near the upper third, using {카피·타이포}; include a campaign title line such as {프로모션명}, a short seasonal message, and a small vertical spine credit reading "HANSSEM HOME COLLECTION 2026" along one side.
3. Feature zone (middle 38%): {제품·소재} displayed in a coherent multi-room sequence, with the sofa and dining set in the foreground, the bed/wardrobe zone suggested through an open doorway or inset lifestyle frame, and small product labels for material, color, and size.
4. Promotion/info zone (lower 22%): structured information block with {행사기간}, {가격혜택}, {매장정보}, {상담CTA}, QR-style consultation box, phone/contact row, online-store note, and small icon-like dividers for delivery, installation, and consultation.
5. Footer/legal strip (bottom 8%): include compact retail disclaimer text {법적고지}, model-name style product codes, and a barcode/receipt-like graphic so the advertisement feels like a real printed promotional poster.
6. Integration rule: {시그니처 결} should visually unify the family moment, room styling, product arrangement, campaign copy, product tags, and price information so the poster feels like one cohesive Korean brand advertisement, not separate cutouts.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard and Noto Sans KR for Korean copy, bold 700 for headline, medium 500 for subcopy, regular 400 for disclaimer; use clean corporate spacing, realistic Korean line breaks, and modest letter spacing for a Hanssem-like retail look.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트} applied as creamy beige background, natural oak warmth, charcoal text, soft blue-gold accent bars, muted terracotta lifestyle accents, and warm ivory panels.
- Graphic system: use thin cool-gray dividers, rounded rectangular product callout tags, small delivery/installation/consultation icons, a QR-style consultation square, barcode graphic, and coupon-like price band without making the layout feel like a discount flyer.
- Text hierarchy: headline must be largest, promotion name second, product benefits third, pricing/contact details smaller but legible; Korean copy should look typeset rather than randomly scattered.
- Material realism: preserve woven upholstery, matte lacquer, oak grain, brushed metal handles, soft bedding folds, ceramic and fabric textures, and natural reflections on floors and tabletops.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 24mm wide-angle interior commercial photography, straightened verticals, f/5.6 look, showroom-scale realism with crisp product edges.
- Lighting: {무드·라이팅}; soft daylight from large windows on the left, gentle fill from the front, warm amber bounce on wood surfaces, readable shadows under furniture, no harsh spotlighting.
- Color grade: warm beige + natural oak + muted charcoal + restrained Hanssem blue/gold accents, slightly soft contrast, polished magazine-ad finish.
- Rendering finish: high-resolution commercial print clarity, realistic paper-poster design overlay, accurate perspective, stable furniture geometry, natural human skin tones, and crisp Korean typography.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean home-furnishing editorial — like a high-end apartment spread from Elle Decor Korea or Architectural Digest Korea combined with a trustworthy Korean retail promotion. Warm, family-centered, practical, aspirational, and believable for a newlywed or young-family apartment.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: "한샘", "HANSSEM", "우리 집이 달라지는 순간", "신혼·가족 라이프 기획전", "2026.05.01 - 2026.05.31", "상담 예약하기", "전국 한샘 디자인파크".
- Recommended rendered copy blocks: headline "우리 집이 달라지는 순간", subheadline "신혼·가족 라이프 기획전", price band "거실·침실·수납 풀패키지 월 79,000원부터", benefit tags "무료 공간 상담", "전문 시공", "맞춤 수납 제안", footer "일부 품목 및 시공 조건에 따라 가격은 달라질 수 있습니다".
- Layout invariants: vertical furniture-ad hierarchy must stay clear; family/home hero at top, products centered, promotion/pricing/contact details at bottom, barcode and QR-style consultation box in the footer area.
- Composition fidelity: preserve the warm Korean home interior advertising feel, with believable family lifestyle details, showroom-grade furniture styling, accurate furniture scale, and polished corporate retail typography.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

[1. PURPOSE]
MUJI-inspired Korean lifestyle advertisement, square hero composition for social media or brand promo use.
Realistic product-centric retail campaign image that feels like a quiet in-store catalog moment with tactile materials, useful everyday objects, and credible shopping information.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the main product cluster in a square hero frame, occupying about 58–65% of the image, with balanced surrounding room for retail copy, price notes, and small catalog details.
- Build a warm lifestyle setting: off-white paper backdrop, pale beige wall, matte tabletop, light wood tray or shelf edge, cotton/linen texture, and subtle natural shadows.
- Place supporting labels, price cues, catalog number, barcode/QR-style area, and store information near the lower corners or side edge, aligned on a clean invisible grid.
- Use {브랜드 톤} as the overall brand voice, with {시그니처 결} reflected in the object selection, material finish, stacking rhythm, paper tags, and fabric textures.
- Build the scene around {제품·소재}, adding realistic companion items such as a folded linen cloth, kraft hangtag, ceramic cup, wooden spoon, cotton pouch, notebook, or small dried branch when they reinforce the everyday retail story.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Hero area (center 60%): arrange {제품·소재} as the primary subject, neatly stacked or slightly offset in a calm showroom-style arrangement, with crisp product edges, believable contact shadows, and tactile surface details.
2) Surface and backdrop: use a matte beige tabletop or pale wood surface with visible fine grain; background stays soft white to warm gray-beige with natural paper fiber, wall corner, faint shelf line, or soft fabric fold.
3) Real retail cues: include a small kraft product tag, simple price label, barcode area, item code, and mini catalog note such as "LIFE GOODS WEEK", "VOL.047", "2026 봄 생활전", "₩12,900부터", and "소재와 쓰임을 생각한 생활용품".
4) Typography zone: place {카피·타이포} in a precise Korean ad layout, using clear hierarchy with a short main copy line such as "나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답" and 2–3 short supporting blurbs like "오래 쓰는 기본", "촉감 좋은 소재", "매일 정돈되는 공간".
5) Additional information strip: add small spine/credit-style text along one side or bottom edge: "Photo: Studio Calm", "Model/Product: Daily Linen Set", "매장 안내 02-0000-2026", "서울시 중구 생활로 12", plus a tiny barcode/QR-style block that reads as retail packaging detail.
6) Layout discipline: keep {레이아웃} with measured spacing, strong alignment, realistic product scale, and a premium retail-catalog feel.
7) Format and output: maintain {비율} as a square composition with balanced breathing room on all sides and enough detail to feel like a photographed lifestyle advertisement.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean copy, paired with a clean sans-serif English title; regular to medium weight, readable small-to-medium hierarchy, tight but natural tracking, clean editorial spacing.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트} interpreted as hex-like tones such as #E8DDCF beige, #F7F4EE white, #B79C7A wood, #3B3A36 charcoal, plus one muted accent from the palette on a tag, label stripe, sticker, or folded fabric edge.
- Retail graphic details: include a small price table, item code line, barcode/QR-style rectangle, date label "2026.05", and short Korean care/material notes, all printed sharply and aligned.
- Shadow and finish: soft realistic product shadows with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, about 12% opacity; matte materials, natural paper fibers, linen weave, ceramic pores, wood grain, and subtle shelf reflections where appropriate.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with RF 85mm f/1.2L lens stopped to f/5.6, studio product photo look, front-facing catalog framing with very low distortion and crisp mid-depth detail.
- Lighting: {무드·라이팅}; diffused natural daylight from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from right, controlled soft shadows, believable highlights on paper, wood, fabric, ceramic, or matte plastic.
- Color grade: warm neutral beige + paper white + light wood brown + soft charcoal, with low saturation, calm contrast, and realistic material separation.

[6. MOOD]
Quiet premium retail campaign — MUJI flagship catalog aesthetics with the restrained clarity of a Japanese lifestyle magazine spread, enriched by tactile everyday objects, believable store information, and Korean lifestyle-ad details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following verbatim Korean strings must appear correctly if shown in the design: "브랜드 톤", "시그니처 결", "제품·소재", "무드·라이팅", "컬러 팔레트", "카피·타이포", "레이아웃", "비율".
- Render short Korean ad text clearly and without corruption, including examples such as "나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답", "오래 쓰는 기본", "촉감 좋은 소재", "매일 정돈되는 공간", "2026 봄 생활전", and "₩12,900부터".
- Maintain a square hero composition with aligned retail typography, believable product scale, natural material textures, and undistorted objects.
- If human figures are included at all, keep them realistic and anatomically correct; otherwise keep the scene product-only.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals or certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean IKEA-style furniture catalog advertisement, approachable retail poster with a room-set hero, product detail modules, realistic prices, and store information.
Vertical catalog ad for furniture promotion, designed to feel like a mass-market Scandinavian home goods print spread with practical shopping cues and lived-in home details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall composition: a tall 1024x1536 retail poster with a dominant upper room-set hero occupying about 55% of the frame, a secondary single-product cutout or close product view at lower-left, and a compact price/store information block at lower-right.
- Background treatment: bright white walls, pale oak wood floor, soft daylight, a woven rug, stacked books, ceramic mug, fabric throw, cushion texture, small framed print, and one or two green plants so the room feels like a real furnished home.
- Spacing and framing: editorial catalog grid with visible module divisions, practical print-ad alignment, a top catalog label strip, lower shopping information area, and readable product callouts connected to the furniture.
- Use {브랜드톤}, {시그니처룩}, {메인제품}, {룸세팅}, {조명분위기}, {컬러팔레트}, {헤드라인}, {모델명}, {가격}, {프로모션문구}, {매장명}, {주소}, {연락처}, {카탈로그번호}, {발행일}, {배송정보}, {레이아웃}, {비율} to control the final retail identity.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Top catalog strip: add a small retail header with {매장명}, {카탈로그번호}, {발행일}, a simple page mark such as “P.18”, and a tiny barcode or QR-style shopping code; keep it believable as a printed catalog page rather than a blank poster.
2) Top hero panel: show a Scandinavian-inspired room scene based on {룸세팅}, with {메인제품} staged naturally in a real home environment; include cushions, lamps, a side table, books, plant leaves, fabric texture, wood grain, and small everyday objects that support the furniture lifestyle.
3) Lower-left product panel: show the featured furniture item from {메인제품} as a catalog cutout, angled close-up, or neat product crop; include material details from the scene such as weave, stitching, wood edge, metal leg, shelf grain, or lamp shade texture.
4) Lower-right information panel: place {헤드라인}, {모델명}, {가격}, {프로모션문구}, {배송정보}, {주소}, and {연락처} in a compact shopping block with price hierarchy, short bullet specs, and a small yellow call-to-action label.
5) Product callouts: add 2–3 small Korean callout labels near the furniture, for example “분리 세탁 커버”, “수납형 구조”, “오늘 배송 가능”, or “원목 무늬 마감”, connected with fine guide lines.
6) Brand treatment: keep the overall retail system aligned with {브랜드톤} and {시그니처룩}, using consistent grid logic, clear product hierarchy, and friendly price-driven catalog communication.
7) Color integration: apply {컬러팔레트} across header strip, price tag, callout dots, small labels, delivery badge, and CTA elements; let the room photography carry natural white, beige, oak, fabric, and plant colors.
8) Typography placement: use the header, model line, price, promo copy, specs, store address, and contact hierarchy with strict alignment, practical line breaks, and clear print readability.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a modern sans-serif such as Noto Sans KR or Pretendard, bold for furniture names and headline, medium for model lines and item specs, and regular for address/contact copy; the price should be prominent and immediately scannable.
- Color palette: use {컬러팔레트} with white as the base, IKEA-like blue as the primary accent, bright yellow as the secondary accent, and beige/wood tones for warmth; use small red or gray micro text only if needed for pricing or delivery notes.
- Catalog graphics: include realistic retail details such as product code, small barcode, QR-style square, page number, discount tag, delivery icon row, material swatch dots, and short spec bullets, all integrated into the grid.
- Border/shadow: use crisp editorial edges with very subtle drop shadows only, around 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, so the cutout/product modules feel clean and realistic.
- Image texture: furniture should show fabric weave, wood grain, seams, screw caps, shelf thickness, cushion compression, paper catalog texture, and natural floor reflections rather than flat vector surfaces.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: high-resolution interior photography look, like a Canon EOS R5 with a 24mm or 35mm lens for the room hero, and an 85mm equivalent for the product cutout to keep proportions clean and commercial.
- Lighting: natural daylight from a large window at upper-left, soft diffuse fill across the room, gentle shadow falloff on the floor, and no harsh contrast.
- Color grade: bright Scandinavian retail grade with white walls, cool blue accents, warm oak wood, restrained yellow highlights, realistic textile texture, and neutral clean whites.

[6. MOOD]
Mass-market Scandinavian retail catalog — friendly home goods brochure and practical showroom print-ad feel, with affordable shopping energy, readable price information, and a believable lived-in room set.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean rendered text must appear correctly and legibly if shown: “{매장명}”, “{헤드라인}”, “{모델명}”, “{가격}”, “{프로모션문구}”, “{배송정보}”, “{주소}”, “{연락처}”, “{카탈로그번호}”, “{발행일}”.
- Include realistic catalog microcopy such as “P.18”, “온라인 전용가”, “재고 확인”, “매장 픽업 가능”, “조립 서비스 별도”, and “QR로 제품 보기” where it fits the layout.
- Keep the composition as a furniture advertisement with a room-set hero on top, product block below-left, and price/store information block below-right.
- Typography must remain legible, aligned, and commercial; no broken Korean characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likeness

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Abstract color moodboard for editorial presentation, designed as a square graphic poster with layered paint textures, palette swatches, studio annotations, and small printed reference labels.
Gallery-magazine style visual reference board that feels like a curated palette study photographed from a real art director’s table, not a single finished painting.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main canvas: full-bleed abstract painted surface occupying most of the frame, with visible brush marks, pigment buildup, dry-brush streaks, scraped edges, paint drag, and tactile canvas or heavy-paper grain.
- Palette chips: small color swatches arranged as a refined secondary row or clustered sample strip, each chip separated by consistent spacing, tiny Korean captions, palette code numbers, and paper-label margins.
- Editorial details: include a small title block reading "추상 컬러 무드보드", issue-style notation such as "VOL.247", date label "2026년 5월호", curator credit "기획: 스튜디오 컬러랩", and tiny texture-note labels like "질감 기록" and "팔레트 샘플".
- Layout balance: one large expressive painted field, one supporting text/label area, one compact swatch zone, and a few realistic art-board details such as crop marks, small tape tabs, registration dots, pencil alignment ticks, or printed sample IDs.
- Use {무드}, {결}, {컬러 팔레트}, {레이아웃}, {타이포}, {결 추가}, {비율} as the configurable visual direction cues.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Base layer: build a textured abstract painting first, using broad opaque strokes, layered translucent washes, visible canvas grain, feathered pigment blooms, and uneven hand-applied paint density across the square composition.
- Color field layer: map the mood into a dominant palette based on {무드}, with 1–2 anchor hues and several supporting tones distributed in large blocks, imperfect gradients, overlapping swaths, rubbed transitions, and visible underpainting.
- Texture layer: emphasize {결} through thick impasto ridges, bristle marks, palette-knife scrapes, cracked dry patches, speckled pigment deposits, and occasional rough areas that reveal underlayers.
- Swatch layer: place small rectangular color chips derived from {컬러 팔레트} in an editorial arrangement; add tiny labels such as "샘플 01", "샘플 02", "톤 기준", "보조색", and concise hex-like or pigment-code marks.
- Typographic layer: apply {타이포} as refined Korean editorial labeling, mixing clean sans-serif captions with small studio-note text; keep the title, date, palette labels, and curator credit legible but subordinate to the painted surface.
- Reference layer: add realistic printed-board information including "MOOD STUDY", "COLOR INDEX", page marker "P.08", a small scale tick strip, and subtle annotation arrows pointing to selected texture areas.
- Finishing layer: add {결 추가} as polished art-book presentation quality, with crisp printed labels, tactile paper fibers, delicate ink registration, and a believable photographed-art-board finish.
- Final framing: maintain {비율} as a centered square composition with rectified overhead perspective, letting the painted field remain dominant while the surrounding editorial marks and labels make it feel like a real curated moodboard page.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, light to regular weight for small notes, medium weight for the title, 18–28px for labels, subtle tracking, with a magazine-reference hierarchy rather than sterile UI text.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} as the direct swatch set; keep neutrals like warm gray #CFC7BC, off-white #F4F1EA, charcoal #2B2B2B, muted kraft paper, and faint graphite only as supporting anchors when needed.
- Surface details: allow realistic paper fibers, matte pigment granulation, small dust specks, faint pencil marks, label-sticker edges, tiny tape shadows, and natural paint thickness variations.
- Border/shadow: avoid heavy framing; if a sheet edge appears, use a faint paper-edge shadow at 3px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity, with subtle crop marks or printed trim indicators for an art-book production feel.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: overhead flat-lay look as if shot with a Phase One IQ4 and 80mm lens at f/8, perfectly rectified square framing.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio lighting from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from lower-right, controlled highlights on raised impasto ridges, preserving matte paint texture and paper relief.
- Color grade: editorial art-book grade with muted pigment realism, balanced contrast, slightly warm neutral whites, and accurate color separation so the palette remains the main visual statement.

[6. MOOD]
Curated gallery-poster moodboard — like a Kinfolk x ARTnews art direction spread with contemporary studio-paint texture, real printed annotations, palette research details, and tactile working-studio authenticity.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: all visible labels must render clean Korean without broken characters.
- Verbatim Korean strings that must appear correctly: "추상 컬러 무드보드", "2026년 5월호", "기획: 스튜디오 컬러랩", "질감 기록", "팔레트 샘플".
- Composition invariant: the image must remain a square abstract moodboard with one large painted field plus small swatches, title block, date/credit labels, and editorial studio notes; do not turn it into a figurative illustration.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header area: set {주제} as the dominant typography, centered or positioned according to {레이아웃}, with large scale, crisp Korean letterforms, and a small issue-style label nearby such as 기획 포스터 05, VOL.247, or 2026년 5월호.
- Middle focal area: build one primary geometric element in the center using {결} as the design direction, with clean edges, a memorable silhouette, and subtle decorative details such as thin orbit lines, small dots, coordinate ticks, cut-paper overlap, or fine halftone texture.
- Lower text area: place a compact supporting line in Korean, for example 오늘의 형태가 내일의 균형이 됩니다, followed by event details such as 2026.05.24 SAT 14:00, 서울 성수 아트홀, 입장권 ₩12,000, 예매 @poster.archive.
- Footer system: add a small sponsor/partner area with believable text marks such as 후원 서울문화재단, 디자인 아카이브, PRINTED IN SEOUL, plus a tiny barcode-like ticket block or catalog code such as P-0524-ART.

- Color application: apply {컬러} as the dominant palette, using the accent color on the focal shape, one small typographic label, sponsor line, or ticket-information marker.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Helvetica Neue, Pretendard, or Noto Sans KR; use bold weight for the headline and regular or medium weight for secondary information; apply {타이포} to guide the exact typographic character, kerning, weight contrast, and line spacing.
- Color palette: follow {컬러} exactly, such as beige + gold or white + black; use restrained contrast with one accent color repeated in a few purposeful details.
- Poster information: include concise Korean event copy such as 전시 안내, 관람 시간 10:00–19:00, 장소 서울 성수 아트홀, 티켓 ₩12,000, and a tiny credit line like 디자인 김하늘 / 사진 없음 / 인쇄 리소프린트.
- Graphic details: add tasteful divider rules, small coordinate numbers, registration crosses, a compact barcode/ticket box, sponsor labels, and subtle paper or ink texture that make the poster feel physically printed.
- Border/shadow: a thin printed edge line, pale crop mark, or soft paper shadow may be used at 10–15% opacity with a subtle 2–4px offset if it supports the realistic poster finish.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

- Lighting: even studio-flat illumination, as if lit from a large diffused softbox directly in front, with controlled soft paper sheen, visible ink density, and no hotspot glare.

- Exact rendered string requirement: {주제}, {레이아웃}, {컬러}, {타이포}, {결 추가} must be rendered cleanly if included as visible Korean text.
- Composition invariant: one dominant headline, one central geometric shape, one structured lower information area, all aligned to a strict poster grid.
- Required realistic poster copy: include short Korean event details such as 전시 안내, 2026.05.24 SAT, 서울 성수 아트홀, 티켓 ₩12,000, 후원 서울문화재단, and a tiny catalog/barcode label.

[1. PURPOSE]

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Square full-bleed ornamental pattern field filling the entire 1024x1024 canvas as a premium Korean heritage graphic.
- Repeating traditional motif system built from {패턴}, arranged as a dense, rhythmic, readable decorative surface.
- Texture layer should feel like {질감}, with visible hanji fiber grain, light ink absorption, and tactile printed-paper warmth.
- Layout should stay {레이아웃}, maintaining balanced symmetry, diagonal rhythm, and carefully varied motif scale across the whole frame.
- Add small museum-goods catalogue details using {타이포}: tiny motif labels, product code, season mark, and archive-style annotations integrated between pattern clusters.
- Include realistic printed souvenir information such as {라벨문구}, {굿즈정보}, and {시즌} as subtle decorative microtext, not as a dominant headline.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Base field: establish a seamless all-over decorative surface that reads like a refined traditional textile, hanji wrapping paper, or museum souvenir packaging sheet.
- Main motifs: distribute {패턴} evenly across the canvas, mixing larger emblem-like dancheong and taegeuk forms with smaller flower, cloud, wave, roof-tile, and bead-like filler shapes.
- Secondary ornament: add fine linework, small rosette repeats, corner-like motif fragments, and soft gold-ink accents so the surface feels crafted rather than flat.
- Texture layer: overlay subtle hanji paper grain, matte ink absorption, faint block-print irregularity, and slight pigment pooling along motif edges, echoing {질감} without reducing clarity.
- Color blocking: apply {컬러} with strong contrast, clean motif separation, and traditional layered color relationships inspired by palace dancheong painting.
- Label accents: insert tiny {타이포} elements such as “{라벨문구}”, “{굿즈정보}”, and “{시즌}” near motif seams, between repeat clusters, or inside small cartouche shapes.
- Print details: include tasteful miniature crop marks, registration dots, swatch chips, archive numbers, and woven-tag inspired rectangles that look like part of a real museum shop pattern sheet.
- Finish: integrate a premium souvenir-poster polish with crisp edges, controlled repetition, tactile paper character, and print-friendly clarity for {비율} output.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Noto Sans KR or Pretendard, medium weight, 12–18px equivalent, compact and museum-label-like for {타이포}; Hanja may appear as tiny decorative annotation when clean and legible.
- Color palette: use the traditional dancheong-inspired mix from {컬러}, with saturated red, deep blue, warm yellow, jade green, off-white, and restrained gold accents.
- Pattern rhythm: combine mirrored symmetry, tiled repetition, and hand-painted imperfections so the design feels like contemporary museum merchandise based on historical Korean ornament.
- Graphic finish: clean vector-like motif boundaries with subtle paper tooth, printed ink density variation, and a refined archive-scan polish.
- Edge treatment: allow the pattern to continue beyond the canvas edges, with occasional small tag panels or motif fragments clipped naturally by the square format.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

- Lighting: even diffuse studio illumination with zero harsh directionality, as if lit by a museum archive lightbox.
- Color grade: vivid dancheong palette with slightly muted paper whites, balanced for screen and print reproduction.
- Material rendering: matte hanji, lightly raised ink, soft pigment texture, and tiny fiber speckles visible at close inspection.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean heritage graphic — museum gift shop pattern sheet meets contemporary cultural editorial design, warm, ceremonial, tactile, and collectible.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: visible microtext must render cleanly, for example “전통문양 아카이브”, “단청 색채 연구”, “궁중문양 굿즈”, “VOL.247”, “2026 봄 컬렉션”, without broken characters.
- All motifs must feel authentically Korean in spirit: dancheong, taegeuk, flower patterns, clouds, waves, roof-tile curves, lotus details, and palace ornament references should remain coherent.
- The composition must stay a seamless all-over traditional pattern sheet, with catalogue labels and product marks supporting the pattern rather than becoming the main subject.
- Printed details such as product code, season label, swatch chips, and archive annotations should look like real museum merchandise design elements.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean city illustration map-style composition for Seoul, combining landmark highlights, neighborhood alley details, and guided-tour editorial information.
Travel-guidebook-style visual that works as a poster, city intro graphic, or editorial spread, with enough real-world information cues to feel like a printed Seoul walking guide.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main composition: {레이아웃} in a 1536x1024 horizontal format, with {랜드마크} distributed as clearly separated illustrated landmarks connected by friendly walking-route lines.
- Subject placement: large landmarks occupy the central city-map flow, while smaller street and neighborhood details fill foreground corners, river edges, and alley pockets with café signs, stair rails, buses, trees, rooftop plants, street lamps, and tiny pedestrians drawn as simple illustration icons.
- Background treatment: layered Seoul cityscape with simplified building blocks, bridges, road curves, Han River shapes, Namsan hillside contours, subway-route hints, and soft paper-grain surface texture.
- Information design: include a title block reading {타이틀}, a small English subtitle {부제}, date label {가이드_날짜}, route name {코스명}, and a compact legend showing 도보, 지하철, 전망, 골목, 카페 icons.
- Label system: landmark names should sit inside small rounded label plaques or map pins, with connecting leader lines, route numbers 01–06, and small English secondary captions under selected Korean labels.
- Style direction: combine cute editorial city-map readability with balanced tourist-guide clarity, using {일러스트_결} and {편집_콘셉트}.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Base scene: build the overall Seoul skyline and district silhouette first, with a low horizon and a wide urban overview that supports the {비율} travel poster format.
2. Landmark layer: place {랜드마크} as the primary visual anchors, each simplified into recognizable shapes and proportions without losing their iconic identity.
3. Street / neighborhood layer: add {골목_디테일} around Hongdae-style streets, palace walls, riverside paths, underpass corners, café awnings, local store signs, crosswalk marks, bicycle racks, and leafy sidewalk details.
4. Route / map layer: draw warm amber route lines, dotted walking paths, subway color dashes, bridge arrows, tiny compass rose, scale bar, and district chips such as 종로, 용산, 송파, 동대문, 마포.
5. Typography layer: apply {타이포} as neat Korean landmark labels, route numbers, micro captions, and one understated English subtitle line beside the main title zone.
6. Editorial detail pass: add {지도_마이크로텍스트}, a small “SEOUL WALKING GUIDE” tag, issue-style note “VOL.247”, page marker “p.08–09”, and a bottom information strip containing {하단정보}.
7. Finish pass: unify all illustration elements with a warm guidebook-like finish, subtle print texture, light shadow separation, and cohesive Seoul travel illustration mood.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean labels, medium weight 500–600, with a simple sans serif English subtitle in a lighter weight; route numbers may use a rounded condensed style for guidebook character.
- Color palette: {컬러팔레트} should be expressed as specific tones such as #E8D8B8 beige, #B68A5A wood brown, #D89A3A amber, #7E9F63 natural green, and dancheong-inspired accent reds/teals used sparingly.
- Illustration linework: clean vector-style outlines, slightly imperfect hand-drawn corners, soft 8%–12% shadow separation, muted paper grain, and small colored badges for landmarks, cafés, transit, and river activities.
- Poster/editorial details: include a compact sponsor/info area styled as travel-guide metadata, not an official government seal; add tiny pictogram icons, caption boxes, route badges, and decorative map ornaments inspired by Seoul streets.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: conceptual city-guide illustration, inspired by an overhead travel map and editorial infographic layout rather than a real camera capture; if perspective is needed, use a wide 24mm architectural viewpoint feel.
- Lighting: even daylight illustration with subtle warm sunlight from upper-left, gentle contrast, and soft shadows under buildings, signs, trees, route plaques, and bridge shapes.
- Color grade: warm cream + amber + beige base with natural green and restrained dancheong color accents, keeping the overall tone airy, readable, and print-friendly.

[6. MOOD]
Travel guidebook editorial illustration — a friendly Seoul city feature with Kinfolk-meets-city-map clarity, lively alley storytelling, and practical walking-tour poster energy.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear correctly in the image: 서울, 서울 산책 지도, 경복궁, N서울타워, 롯데월드타워, 동대문 DDP, 한강, 홍대.
- Additional rendered Korean details should include: 2026 서울 여행 노트, 오늘의 코스, 도보 3시간, 종로, 용산, 송파, 동대문, 마포, 카페거리, 한강공원.
- Korean labels, captions, route chips, and bottom information text must be crisp, evenly spaced, and fully legible with no broken or mirrored characters.
- Composition must remain a Seoul landmark-and-alley illustration with real Seoul cues; do not replace with unrelated cities, fantasy landmarks, or generic non-Seoul streets.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public figures
- Misleading official government/emergency insignia

[1. PURPOSE]
Geometric pattern art poster, abstract shape composition for modern editorial, exhibition, and wall-art use.
Full-frame square poster built from circles, triangles, grids, lines, dots, and waves with a polished contemporary graphic identity, including realistic exhibition-poster information and collectible print details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Canvas is filled edge-to-edge with {패턴} as the main subject, creating a dense and visually complete square artwork.
- Overall structure uses {레이아웃}: modular zones, diagonal rhythm, repeated shape clusters, and layered wave or grid accents that make the poster feel intentionally composed.
- Visual language follows {디자인결}, so the surface feels crisp, editorial, and print-ready rather than painterly.
- Main shapes should be arranged in a stable modular system, with repeated forms aligned cleanly across the square frame while allowing a few playful overlaps, cropped circles, and stepped line groups.
- Color treatment uses {컬러} with strong contrast control, consistent saturation, and 1–2 accent colors reserved for hierarchy.
- Add realistic poster typography: a Korean exhibition title {전시명}, edition code {에디션}, date/time line {행사정보}, venue {장소}, ticket line {티켓}, host credit {주최}, and sponsor strip {스폰서}.
- Typography should follow {타이포스타일}; text may run vertically along one side, sit inside a small label block, or align to the grid as part of the artwork.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Base field: build a full-bleed square composition that feels like a designed art poster, with graphic elements reaching the edges and key text held inside a readable poster-safe zone.
- Pattern layer: render {패턴} as the dominant visual language, mixing geometric repetition, line logic, dot matrices, modular spacing, and wave bands so the whole image reads as one cohesive system.
- Rhythm layer: vary scale and density across the canvas to create movement: large cropped circles, thin parallel lines, checkerboard micro-grids, triangular markers, dotted constellations, and wave ribbons.
- Color layer: apply {컬러} as a refined palette with one dominant background tone, one strong structural color, and one bright accent for title or wayfinding labels.
- Information layer: include {전시명} as the main Korean title, {에디션} as a collectible art-print mark, and compact lines for {행사정보}, {장소}, and {티켓}.
- Sponsor / credit layer: place {주최} and {스폰서} in a small footer or side rail, separated by fine divider rules, small dots, or geometric icons.
- Style reference layer: emphasize {디자인결} influence in the geometry, using clean circles, grid logic, disciplined spacing, and bold modernist proportions.
- Final finish: keep edges crisp, surfaces smooth, ink-like, and print-flat, with subtle paper grain or risograph-like registration texture only if it supports a believable poster print.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard, Noto Sans KR, or a clean geometric sans-serif; mix bold title text with regular-weight information lines, approximately 10–48px equivalent depending on hierarchy.
- Korean title treatment: {전시명} should be highly legible, set horizontally or vertically with correct spacing and natural Korean typography.
- Color palette: use the exact feel of {컬러}, such as pastel lavender, mint, blush, sky blue, charcoal, gold, coral, cyan, cream, or warm gray; keep saturation controlled and avoid muddy blends.
- Decorative graphics: include small registration marks, numbered ticks, micro arrows, circular labels, thin divider lines, or wave badges that belong naturally to an art poster.
- Border/shadow: if separation is needed, use fine graphic rules, inset label panels, or gentle 6–10% shadow on text panels while maintaining a flat poster impression.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: simulated flat graphic artwork, top-down poster layout, no perspective distortion, no photographic depth of field.
- Lighting: even studio-like illumination with print-flat clarity and clean color separation.
- Color grade: modern graphic palette with crisp contrast, soft pastel balance, or bold Bauhaus-style primary accents depending on {컬러}.
- Rendering: vector-clean edges, sharp typography, believable screen-print or fine paper texture, precise alignment, and square 1024x1024 composition.

[6. MOOD]
{분위기} — a contemporary Korean design-festival poster, Bauhaus and Material Design inspired, like a collectible museum shop print with real exhibition details and lively abstract motion.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 한글 정확.
- Visible Korean text must be clean and readable, especially “{전시명}”, “{행사정보}”, “{장소}”, “{티켓}”, “{주최}”.
- Suggested rendered copy may include: “기하의 리듬”, “2026.05.24–06.14”, “서울 성수 디자인홀 B1”, “입장 ₩7,500”, “EDITION 024”.
- Keep the composition fully geometric and abstract; text and decorative marks are allowed as poster design elements, but do not introduce figurative imagery.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters
- People, faces, hands, animals, or any figurative subject
- Photographic realism, 3D mockup styling, or glossy AI-smoothed surfaces

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
보태닉 일러스트 포스터 / 식물·꽃 컬렉션 편집 디자인. 2x3 grid or free collage layout for editorial wall art, printable poster, botanical exhibition poster, and social-media share.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall framing: a tall 1024x1536 vertical poster with {레이아웃} as the main structure, designed like a vintage botanical art exhibition sheet with editorial poster information integrated into the artwork.
- Subject placement: six botanical illustrations distributed across the page with clear visual hierarchy; larger focal blooms near the upper-left and lower-right, smaller leaf specimens woven between labels, captions, date blocks, and decorative specimen marks.
- Background treatment: warm cream-beige paper texture with visible fibrous grain, light archival stains, faint print speckles, and subtle pressed-flower shadows that make the poster feel physically printed.
- Poster information layer: include the exhibition title “{전시명}”, date “{행사일정}”, time “{행사시간}”, venue “{장소}”, ticket line “{티켓정보}”, and a small sponsor/archive area “{후원문구}”.
- Editorial details: add specimen numbers, Latin-style plant names, Korean plant labels, page-like folio marks, a small barcode-style inventory mark, and delicate botanical diagram lines without overwhelming the six featured plants.
- Apply {결} as the underlying art direction, and keep {결_추가} influence visible through magazine-like section labels, herbarium annotations, and refined printed finishing.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Canvas base — set an off-white cream paper field with faint natural fiber texture, lightly aged edges, tiny ink flecks, and a scanned archival herbarium-sheet feeling.
2. Primary botanical set — place {식물목록} as six distinct illustrated subjects, each with nearby Korean name, Latin-inspired caption, specimen number, and one small descriptive note such as “개화”, “향”, or “잎맥”.
3. Layout system — arrange the six pieces according to {레이아웃}: either a structured 2x3 grid with editorial gutters or a loose collage with slight rotation, overlapping stems, label stickers, thin guide lines, and herbarium tape details while keeping all six plants readable.
4. Poster title block — position “{전시명}” prominently near the upper area, with a smaller subtitle “식물과 꽃의 기록전” and the short curator note “{소개문구}”.
5. Event detail block — place “{행사일정} · {행사시간} · {장소}” in a neat information band; add “{티켓정보}” as a ticket/call-to-action line near the lower third or bottom.
6. Sponsor and archive strip — include “{후원문구}”, a small barcode-style code “BOT-{포스터번호}”, and a printed credit line “Illustrated Botanical Archive / Seoul” near the bottom edge.
7. Color handling — render all flora using {컬러} as the governing palette, with soft watercolor washes, ink outlines, muted shadowing, pressed-petal stains, and restrained vintage print contrast.
8. Typography layer — apply {타이포} as delicate label text near each plant, resembling vintage botanical specimen tags with Korean lettering, Latin serif captions, and small event typography.
9. Finishing pass — add fine rule lines, tiny decorative flower icons, specimen arrows, transparent washi-tape corners, and subtle overprint texture inspired by {결_추가}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean labels and event details, paired with a thin Latin serif such as Cormorant Garamond or Baskerville; use readable hierarchy with 18–28 px specimen labels, 34–52 px poster title, and smaller 12–16 px archive notes.
- Rendered Korean text examples in the poster: “{전시명}”, “식물과 꽃의 기록전”, “{행사일정}”, “{행사시간}”, “{장소}”, “{티켓정보}”, “{후원문구}”, “장미 Rosa”, “라벤더 Lavender”, “올리브 Olive”.
- Color palette: {컬러} should resolve into botanical greens, floral signature accents, warm cream beige, aged ink brown, and softened leaf-shadow gray; recommend tones like #EDE4D1, #7C9B74, #D98C8C, #C9B07A, #5E6F58, and #6D5A45.
- Border/shadow: use a printed poster edge, fine hairline rules, pinned-paper shadows, and soft herbarium tape overlays; shadows should feel like physical paper layers photographed in daylight.
- Decorative graphics: include tiny seed diagrams, leaf cross-section icons, dotted measuring ticks, archival catalog numbers, and small floral corner ornaments that match the botanical theme.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial flat-lay look, equivalent to a top-down 50mm lens perspective with no perspective distortion, as if photographed for a modern herbarium catalog.
- Lighting: even diffused daylight from upper-left, soft fill from right, gentle paper-layer shadows, visible watercolor pigment blooms, ink texture, and cream paper grain throughout.
- Color grade: muted natural greens, dusty petal tones, warm cream paper, slightly desaturated vintage print contrast, and a tactile museum-shop poster finish.

[6. MOOD]
Vintage botanical magazine spread meets small gallery exhibition poster — poetic, collectible, archival, and handmade, like a refined museum catalog plate printed for a spring botanical art fair.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered image must preserve clean, correct Korean lettering wherever labels, event details, and captions appear; no broken characters, no missing glyphs.
- Must visually communicate six botanical subjects in one cohesive collection page: “장미”, “해바라기”, “라벤더”, “올리브”, “유칼립투스”, “몬스테라”.
- Required visible Korean poster text: “{전시명}”, “{행사일정}”, “{행사시간}”, “{장소}”, “{티켓정보}”, “{후원문구}”.
- Labels should remain elegant and legible, with botanical illustration details, specimen numbers, and archive-style captions supporting the poster rather than hiding the plants.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or garbled botanical labels
- Celebrity composites / real-person likeness insertion
- AI-smooth plastic rendering that removes watercolor, ink, and paper texture

studio:prompts3:ours-714.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Modern Bauhaus-inspired art poster for an exhibition announcement, editorial wall print, and design portfolio showcase.
Create a real, content-rich vertical poster with geometric abstraction, bold Korean typography, practical event information, ticket details, sponsor area, and authentic print-production cues.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Canvas is a vertical exhibition poster where the main geometric cluster occupies about 55% of the frame and sits slightly above center for a museum-poster balance, with additional information blocks arranged on a precise modular grid.
- Background treatment: matte white or warm off-white paper surface with visible fine paper grain, subtle ink absorption, slight CMYK registration character, and a printed-poster finish.
- Use {결}, {구성}, {텍스트}, {컬러}, {타이포}, {결 추가} as customizable creative directions while keeping the layout structured, editorial, and poster-like.
- The composition should feel grid-based and modular: align circles, triangles, rectangles, rules, numeric labels, and sponsor marks to an invisible Bauhaus grid with precise spacing, sharp edges, measured visual tension, and believable printed detail.
- Include practical poster content: exhibition title, short subtitle, date/time/venue, ticket price, website or contact line, sponsor strip, and small archival catalog text.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Upper zone (top 18%): place the main title text block in a clean header area using compact tracking and strong grid alignment. Let {텍스트} appear as the largest Korean typographic statement, supported by smaller lines such as '바우하우스 기하학전', '선과 면의 리듬', and 'VOL.014'.
- Central zone (middle 50%): build the primary abstract structure from circles, triangles, squares, rectangles, thin black rules, and modular numeric markers. Use one dominant shape as the anchor and smaller shapes orbiting with controlled asymmetry; allow overlapping flat color fields, visible overprint edges, and light ink registration offsets.
- Secondary balance points: add smaller geometric accents, section numbers, thin divider lines, and micro labels near the lower-left and upper-right areas to stabilize the design and make it feel like a finished exhibition print.
- Information zone (lower 25%): include event details in Korean, arranged with strict hierarchy: '2026.05.01–05.31', '화–일 10:00–18:00', '서울 디자인 아카이브 3층', '입장권 ₩7,500', '문의 02-714-2026', and 'www.designarchive.kr'.
- Sponsor / credit strip: place a small bottom strip with simple wordmark-style text such as '주최 디자인랩', '후원 서울문화재단', '협력 타이포그래피 연구소', plus a tiny barcode-like ticket block or catalog code 'BAU-714'.
- Text integration: {텍스트} should appear as a prominent typographic statement, set with modern industrial clarity and exact legibility, integrated as part of the poster design rather than a separate caption.
- Color application: use {컬러} as the explicit palette logic, assigning bold flat color fills to geometric shapes, with subtle print grain, overprint touches, and slight ink density variation for realism.
- Typography treatment: {타이포} should appear in a Bauhaus-informed sans-serif arrangement, with bold weight for the main phrase, medium weight for event details, and tiny condensed text for credits and catalog notes.
- Texture cue: {결 추가} may be expressed as paper grain, ink bleed at edges, faint halftone speckling, letterpress-like pressure, or analog screen-print registration detail.
- Format control: {비율} defines a tall poster layout with crisp vertical flow and a complete exhibition-poster hierarchy.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Helvetica Neue or Arial-inspired grotesk, bold weight for headline, medium weight for secondary text, condensed small caps feeling for credits, with tight but readable line spacing and precise geometric alignment.
- Color palette: Bauhaus signature palette with red #E53935, yellow #F4C430, blue #1E5AA8, black #111111, and white #F7F5EF; maintain {컬러} as the active palette direction.
- Graphic detail: use thin black rules, numbered grid coordinates, small catalog labels, ticket-code blocks, and sponsor text to create the impression of a professionally printed exhibition poster.
- Print realism: include slight paper waviness, natural ink density changes, mild registration offset, and tiny edge imperfections while keeping the poster front-facing and legible.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing graphic poster render, equivalent to an 85mm straight-on product shot feel with zero distortion, perfectly orthographic and centered.
- Lighting: even studio light from the front with soft diffuse coverage, faint paper-surface relief, and gentle print-like edge separation.
- Color grade: clean neutral whites, saturated primary accents, high contrast black text, and slightly muted paper warmth for a gallery-print finish.

[6. MOOD]
Museum-quality Bauhaus exhibition poster — disciplined, historical, tactile, and editorial, like a well-preserved design archive print prepared for a contemporary Korean gallery event.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: no broken Korean characters in any supporting labels or custom text.
- Render Korean poster copy clearly, including {텍스트} plus supporting text such as '바우하우스 기하학전', '선과 면의 리듬', '2026.05.01–05.31', '서울 디자인 아카이브 3층', '입장권 ₩7,500', and '주최 디자인랩'.
- Layout invariant: maintain a strict geometric grid, flat Bauhaus color logic, balanced asymmetry, and a complete exhibition-poster information system.
- The design must preserve the original concept of a modern art poster with Bauhaus and constructivist geometry while feeling like a real printed event poster.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-713.content:
